Hidratación: ácido hialurónico, aminoácidos y péptidos
Folículo piloso y ciclo del cabello
Desarrollo de producto y marketing de fragancias
Intelligent Targeting Carrier / Poly(lactic-co-glycolic acid) / Polyvinyl Alcohol
Omega-7 Fatty Acids / Macadamia Nut Oil / Sea Buckthorn Oil
In Vitro Epithelial Cell Models / Alternatives to Animal Testing / Rosette Test
Enzyme Biology-Based Skin Care Marketing / Papain / Bromelain
Hayflick's Entropy View of Aging / Strehler's Criteria of Aging

nodes.label: The Skin: Structure, Biochemistry, and Function

summaries.text: Comprehensive overview of skin morphology, the epidermal keratinizing system, terminal differentiation, pigmentation, dermis, appendages, hair and nails. It covers barrier function and penetration pathways of cosmetic actives, immunology, cytokines, enzymes, UV-induced photodamage and skin cancer, and gene expression (genomics) in skin care.

nodes.label: Sustainability and Eco-Responsibility: A Global Approach

summaries.text: Covers Part 12 of the sustainability focus book: defining sustainability and open innovation for sustainability, a botanist's view of sustainable wild harvesting and benefit sharing, the Herboretum network, local cultivation for carbon footprint reduction, plant cell cultures producing phenylpropanoids, eco-responsible plant extraction and formulation, and green industrial solutions like zeodration and wetland gardens.

nodes.label: Changing Regulatory Landscape in the U.S. and E.U.

summaries.text: Overview of US (FD&C Act, FPLA) and EU (Regulation 1223/2009) cosmetic regulation: definitions, classification, labeling, INCI, safety assessment, GMP, PIF/CPSR, CPNP notification, RAPEX and REACH. Concludes that simultaneous compliance is possible since EU compliance largely satisfies US guidelines.

nodes.label: Molecular Cell Biology and Gene Analysis for Cosmetics

summaries.text: Introduces molecular cell biology for cosmetic chemists: proteins and amino acids, cell organelles, cell signaling and receptor classes, and epigenetics (DNA methylation, histone modification). Applies these to skin care via skin immunity, gene expression analysis and the Nrf2 and AMPK pathways activated by phytochemicals such as resveratrol and sulforaphane.

nodes.label: Creating the Right Fragrance for Your Personal Care Product

summaries.text: Guide to working with a fragrance house (perfumer-evaluator teams, library, QC) and to fragrance composition: natural and synthetic materials, top/middle/base notes, volatility, log Kow and odor thresholds. Also covers use-cycle evaluation, cost and carriers, troubleshooting color/stability/odor, EU 26 allergen labeling and fragrance types such as WS, WD, INCI blends, natural and GRAS fragrances.

Reviews skin structure and the effects of intrinsic and extrinsic (photo) aging on the stratum corneum, epidermis and dermis, including barrier function, TEWL, dry skin, mechanical properties, telangiectasia and photo-aging mechanisms. Covers treatments: sunscreens, tretinoin and cosmeceuticals (retinol, niacinamide, hydroxy acids, antioxidants, peptides).
Age-related change in appearance that consumers seek to reverse; gene expression studies give insight into its mechanisms and DNA methylation plays a role in sun-exposed aging skin.
Age-related skin changes divided into intrinsic and extrinsic aging; wrinkles and color inhomogeneity drive apparent age.

Age changes include lower elasticity and tensile strength, reduced dermal and epidermal thickness, vascularity, hydration and sensory perception, flattened DEJ, increased permeability and slower wound healing.
Preventing aging is described as a major area driven by the escalating senior population.
Natural progressive process of the skin determined by intrinsic and extrinsic factors.

nodes.label: Glycation, Proteasome Activation, and Telomere Maintenance

summaries.text: Reviews glycation (AGE formation, measurement by AGE-Reader autofluorescence, anti-glycation and deglycation ingredients incl. Albizia julibrissin), the proteasome/UPS and autophagy as cellular clearance targets, and telomere/telomerase/shelterin biology with cosmetic telomere-protecting actives. Stresses the three topics are interconnected.

Presents cellular anti-senescence as a 'single-bullet' skin anti-aging approach. Covers senescence vs apoptosis, enzyme dysfunction (oxidative stress, peroxisomes, immunosenescence, AGEs, ubiquitin-proteasome system, MFRTA), anhydrobiosis and osmoprotection, new osmoprotective glutaminylglutamine amide peptide derivatives with formulations, and consumer marketing of enzyme biology.

nodes.label: Mechanisms of Changes in Hair Shape

summaries.text: Treats hair as a shape memory biopolymer and explains temporary and permanent shape changes by water-setting, hot irons, thioglycolate perms and alkaline relaxers via a three-step soften-impose-lock mechanism. Also covers grooming dynamics, volume, frizz, body and styling polymers (Tg, welding seams, adhesion).

Reviews alpha-hydroxy acids (glycolic, lactic, citric, mandelic) and their clinical and mechanistic effects across stratum corneum, epidermis and dermis, then second- and third-generation polyhydroxy and bionic acids, N-acetylamino sugars and N-acetylamino acids. Details low-pH formulation strategies (pKa, thickeners, emulsifiers, amphoteric complexes) to balance efficacy and irritation.

Covers production (fermentation, enzymatic, extraction), properties and derivatives of amino acids and their benefits against signs of skin and hair aging: wrinkling, elasticity, clarity, hydration, UV damage, hair breakage, dullness and roughness. Includes example cleanser, moisturizer, serum, shampoo and conditioner formulations.

Explains epigenetic principles (DNA methylation, chromatin remodeling and histone modification), their links to aging, epigenetic drift in aging skin illustrated by identical twins, DNA damage repair, cosmetic ingredients and dietary compounds as epigenetic modifiers (nutriepigenetics), and epigenetics as a possible unifying theory of aging.
Major dermal fiber (75% of dry weight, 18-30% of volume) rich in glycine, hydroxyproline and hydroxylysine; made by fibroblasts from procollagen; vitamin C and copper are cofactors.
Dermal protein; stem cells and their factors increase collagen content and synthesis.
Critical ECM protein broken down in inflammation-driven aging; protected by curcuminoids.
Structural protein (types I, IV etc.) synthesized by fibroblasts; type I forms trabeculae supporting fat.
Dermal structural protein; retinoids increase new collagen formation.
Skin structural protein that is attacked by glucose in glycation, forming AGEs.
Ultraviolet light activates keratinocyte inflammasomes and inflammatory pathways and is a form of barrier disruption.
Ultraviolet radiation causes photodamage, premature aging, immunosuppression, DNA mutations and skin cancer; a complete carcinogen (initiator and promoter).
Ultraviolet sunlight that oxidizes hair proteins, lipids and melanin, causing photo-aging, lightening, brittleness and follicle damage.
UVA/UVB environmental stressor triggering ROS and inflammatory cascade.
Ultraviolet light that stimulates keratinocytes to signal melanin production and causes pyrimidine dimer DNA damage.
Retinoid use increases sensitivity to ultraviolet radiation so sunscreen is recommended.
External trigger of inflammation and additive influence on skin aging.

Explains intrinsic and extrinsic hair aging and its signs: thinning, graying, dryness, loss of shine and manageability, and photo-aging. Gives scalp and hair care advice and surveys anti-aging hair ingredients (minoxidil, glycolic acid, coconut oil, L-arginine, UV filters) and market products.
Skin aging sign; cited as target of patented new-use example.
Visible sign of aging; crow's feet number peaks about age 35 while depth increases eightfold from 35 to 65.
Sign of skin aging; ADSC injection and topical secreted factors showed anti-wrinkle effects.
HA fragments treat and prevent wrinkles; decline of HA with age leads to wrinkles.
Lines from aging; reduced by Laminaria extract and filled by marine EPS and silicone elastomers.
Fine facial wrinkles are an FDA-approved indication for tretinoin.
Age-related sign caused by collagen cross-linking and inflammation-derived free radical damage to collagen and elastin.

Introduces microRNA biology (discovery, nomenclature, biogenesis, RISC-mediated silencing) and reviews microRNA roles in epidermal differentiation, pigmentation, dermal fibroblasts, adipocytes, hair follicles and senescence. Discusses use of reconstructed skin models to evaluate anti-aging ingredients via microRNA studies.

nodes.label: Physical and Chemical Properties of Hair

summaries.text: Reviews hair chemical composition, cortical, cuticle and medulla cells, viscoelasticity, shape memory, moisture sorption, optical properties and melanin, linking structure to hair function. Closes with follicle zones and the anagen-catagen-telogen life cycle, arguing hair proteins retain biological activity.

Covers causes of UV-induced oxidative damage (photosensitizers, ROS/RNS, NADPH oxidase, free metals), the skin's endogenous antioxidant network, and consequences for MMPs, ECM and the dermal-epidermal junction. Reviews conventional and nonconventional antioxidants (tocopherol, vitamin C, carotenoids, polyphenols, emblica, resveratrol, bakuchiol, retinoids, hexylresorcinol, antioxidant-photostabilizers) and combinations.

Describes the anatomy of the anagen hair follicle (infundibulum, isthmus, bulge, bulb, dermal papilla, root sheaths) and the cycle of anagen, catagen, telogen, exogen and kenogen with its molecular regulators. Also covers follicle aging: graying via melanocyte loss and oxidative stress, and UV damage to follicles.

nodes.label: Intellectual Property: Patents and Trade Secrets

summaries.text: Guide to intellectual property for cosmetics: utility, design and plant patents, utility models, patentability criteria, PCT and regional patent systems, trade secrets, trademarks, trade dress and copyright. Also covers freedom to operate, partnering, infringement types, traditional knowledge (TKDL) and patent/trademark searching.

Explains silicone polymers from silanes and polydimethylsiloxanes to organosilicone copolymers, resins and crosspolymers, using M/D/T/Q nomenclature. Covers solubility, surface tension, volatile silicones and cyclomethicone replacements, dimethicone copolyols, alkyl and multi-domain silicones, alkyl dimethicone copolyol emulsifiers, and the Green Star Rating for greening formulations.

Traces the history of skin whitening products in Japan and the quasi-drug regulatory system, listing approved whitening actives (placenta, vitamin C derivatives, kojic acid, arbutin, ellagic acid, tranexamic acid, etc.) with their mechanisms. Reviews targets in melanocytes, keratinocytes, nerves and corneocytes, from tyrosinase inhibition to MITF, POMC, Substance P and PAR-2.
Molecules that Harman (1956) proposed cause indiscriminate oxidative damage not always neutralized by antioxidants; Nrf2 protects against ROS damage.
Their measurement can be interfered with by nanomaterials.
Oxidants generated by UVB/UVA that indirectly damage DNA and drive photoaging.
ROS accumulate up to millimolar levels in gray/white scalp follicles and cause free radical damage to follicle melanocytes.
Free radicals directly scavenged by phenylpropanoids and their glycosides.
Damage DNA, proteins, lipids, saccharides; increased by pollution, UV, stress, smoking; drive inflammation and premature aging.
Damage cells by oxidizing membrane phospholipids, proteins and nucleic acids; controlled by endogenous antioxidant systems.
Oxygen radicals; by-products of mitochondrial metabolism that damage mitochondrial DNA.

nodes.label: Theories of Aging: Skin Anti-Aging at the Tipping Point

summaries.text: Reviews fifteen mainstream theories of aging, grouped into DNA damage theories and built-in (programmed) breakdown theories. Concludes the most established are free radical, mitochondrial, hormonal and telomere theories, with no unified theory and caloric restriction the only intervention shown to slow cellular time (in non-humans).

Presents oral anatomy, physiology and microbiology (teeth, gums, saliva, dental deposits) and the biology of major oral problems: plaque, calculus, caries, erosion, periodontal disease, hypersensitivity, staining, malodor, xerostomia and canker sores. Reviews cosmetic and OTC drug approaches such as fluorides, antimicrobials, desensitizers and bleaching agents.

Overview of Chinese cosmetic regulation for importers: special vs non-special use categories, CFDA registration documents, mandatory animal testing, impurity-focused safety assessment, comparison with the EU, and the IECIC existing ingredient inventory with slow new-ingredient approval.
Cellular aging state linked with aging and cancer; H2O2-induced premature keratinocyte senescence was prevented by resveratrol via AMPK.
Delayed in skin stem cells by apple meristem extracts.
Aging state of fibroblasts marked by beta-galactosidase; reversed by Laminaria extract.
Irreversible cell cycle arrest during aging regulated by p53-p21 and p16-pRB pathways; modulated by senescence-associated microRNAs.
State where cells stop replicating; its reversal is believed to be an important function of anti-aging products.

Part 1 explains normal sleep stages, chronic stress via the HPA axis, insomnia and obstructive sleep apnea, and how poor sleep, cortisol, epinephrine, reduced growth hormone and free radicals accelerate skin aging; therapies include CBT, sleep hygiene, CPAP and oral appliances. Part 2 presents epigenetic orthodontics, using functional appliances and mechanotransduction to remodel craniofacial bone as nonsurgical facial anti-aging.
Excess melanin causing dark spots; common precaution for olive and darker EP classes, especially with excessive sun exposure.
Pigmentation disorders such as melasma, chloasma, age spots and freckles.
Excess pigmentation such as freckles, age spots, melasma and post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation targeted by whitening quasi-drugs.
Pigmentary disorders treated adjunctively by retinoids via tyrosinase blocking, desquamation and increased turnover.
Aging-skin sign with epigenetic regulation; target for epigenetic treatments.

nodes.label: Nanomaterials in Cosmetics: Regulatory and Safety

summaries.text: Reviews regulation of nanomaterial-containing cosmetics in Europe (6-month pre-notification, [nano] labeling, SCCS guidance), the US (FDA draft guidance, no premarket approval) and Canada (notification, hotlist, NSNR under CEPA). Discusses safety assessment issues: study design, physicochemical characterization, dose metrics and assay interference.

nodes.label: Natural and Synthetic Polymers: Designing Rheological Properties

summaries.text: Surveys rheological additives for aqueous systems (gums, cellulosics, starch derivatives, clays, PEGs, fatty alcohols, synthetic polymers) and nonaqueous systems (silicas, polyethylenes, fatty acids, castor oil derivatives, organoclays). Explains thixotropic vs pseudoplastic behavior, yield value, emulsion stabilization, suspension, foam, lubricity and conditioning functions and how to select additives.
Premature skin aging from UV exposure: leathery thickened outer shell, mottled pigmentation, sagging and wrinkles.
Skin damage from UVA and UVB exposure, mitigated by amla.
Dermal photoaging from UV-induced MMP-1; THC with tetrahydropiperine reversed photodamage in 3-month trial.
Skin damage from chronic sun exposure: epidermal thinning, dysplasia, wrinkles, mottled pigmentation; ameliorated by topical retinoids.

nodes.label: Dermatologic Disorders in Skin of Color

summaries.text: Reviews disorders more common or more noticeable in skin of color, framed by Fitzpatrick phototypes: melasma, post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation, vitiligo, idiopathic guttate hypomelanosis and pseudofolliculitis barbae, with their causes and treatments (hydroquinone, natural lighteners, phototherapy, etc.).

nodes.label: Specialty Corrective Cosmeceuticals for Asian Ethnic Skin

summaries.text: Defines the Asian ethnic skin market (EP classes V-VII) and the cultural demand for fair skin driving a large skin-lightening market in India, China and Japan. Explains melanin differences (pheomelanin yellow undertones), common pigmentary and other conditions of ethnic skin, preventive regimens and treatments (exfoliation, peels, microdermabrasion, IPL, sunscreen).
Ingredients developed further after WWII; in molecular terms antioxidants cannot always fully neutralize ROS damage (Harman).
Molecules that help the stratum corneum regenerate and protect itself and underlying layers from UV and environmental toxins.
Compounds scavenging reactive species and chelating metals; phenylpropanoids and rosemary extract act as antioxidants.
Herbal antioxidants protect skin from ROS; Ayurvedic sources rich in vitamin C, phenolic acids and bioflavonoids.
Compounds that inhibit oxidation; can block tyrosinase-driven oxidation steps of melanogenesis.
Substances that at low concentration significantly delay or prevent oxidation of a substrate (Halliwell and Gutteridge); quench free radicals and can slow signs of aging.
Exogenous antioxidant supplementation needed as endogenous defenses decline during senescence.
Sun-screening agents were developed in WWII for men marooned on liferafts or in deserts facing severe solar exposure, a stimulus for cosmetic science.
Classified as a drug in the US (sunscreen ingredients used only for product color protection must be qualified) but as a cosmetic in the EU.
OTC products with UV-absorbing agents that help lower the incidence of skin cancer.
UV filters in shampoos, conditioners and sprays that prevent keratin breakdown and dye fading, e.g. Crodasorb UV-HPP, PARSOL SLX, ChromAveil.
Uses phosphate ester and silicone copolyol emulsifiers and dispersants for inorganic particles.
Sun protection product; rheological film formers help distribute actives and improve water resistance; cetyl dimethicone raises SPF via uniform films.
Recommended during topical retinoid use due to increased UV sensitivity.
Enzyme in melanosomes catalyzing melanin formation by oxidation of tyrosine to DOPA and DOPAquinone.
Rate-limiting enzyme of melanogenesis oxidizing tyrosine; H2O2-mediated oxidation of its methionine limits function and leads to graying.
Enzyme inhibited by algal compounds, fucoxanthin and peptides for skin lightening.
Copper-containing glycoprotein enzyme in melanosomes catalyzing tyrosine hydroxylation to DOPA and DOPA to dopaquinone; primary whitening target.
Melanogenic enzyme whose transcription is blocked by retinoids.
Melanogenic enzyme whose degradation may be accelerated by increased proteasome activity.
Major glycosaminoglycan of the dermal ground substance; very high molecular weight and water-binding.
Advancement in hyaluronic acid is cited as a breakthrough ingredient technology.
Hydrolyzed hyaluronic acid used in serums and shampoos.

Q&A overview of Russian and Customs Union cosmetic market access under Technical Regulation TR CU 009/2011 (in force July 1, 2012), which replaced dual State Registration plus GOST R certification with a single document. Compares CU requirements with EU rules and notes Russia's WTO accession.
Epidermal cell acting as a sensor of danger from pathogens, irritants and toxins; UV activates its inflammasomes.
Main epidermal cell type (about 95% of epidermis) producing keratin and cytokines; matures outward from the basal layer to become corneocytes.
Basal keratinocyte HA is intracellular and involved in cell cycling.
Epidermal cell that, stimulated by UV, signals melanocytes via alpha-MSH and endothelin to supply melanin.
Main epidermal cell type whose differentiation is regulated by miR-203, miR-24 and others.
Epidermal cell; senescent keratinocytes accumulate with age.
Enzymes activated by UVA that break down collagen and elastic tissue, causing sagging and wrinkles.
Increased by inflammatory cascade, contributing to ECM breakdown.
Zinc-containing enzymes (collagenases, gelatinases, stromelysins, MT-MMPs) secreted as proenzymes into ECM that cleave collagen; inhibited by TIMPs.
MMP1 is a major collagen-degrading protease targeted by miR-92a.
MMP1 activity inhibited by avocado peptide complex.
Cellular stress from oxidation; Nrf2 signals protection against it, though it is one factor of multifactorial stress resistance.
Imbalance of reactive oxygen species over antioxidant defenses; damages hair fibers and follicle melanocytes and is implicated in graying and hair aging.
UV-induced oxidative stress increases MMP expression and collagen degradation.
UVB-induced oxidative stress in fibroblasts prevented by ASCs.
Chronic oxidant stress, alongside inflammation, ravages aging skin.

nodes.label: Saudi Arabia Cosmetics Market Access and Regulations

summaries.text: Overview of cosmetic regulation in the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia under the SFDA: sanctioned Gulf standard GSO 1943/2009, SFDA product classification guidance with extra ingredient restrictions, labeling rules (Arabic, country of origin, no medical claims) and shipment-based Certificate of Conformity market access.

Proposes that cellulite results from estrogen-triggered MMP-1 collagenase destruction of type I collagen trabeculae in thigh and buttock fat, linked to the menstrual cycle. Recommends topical anti-estrogens (genistein, chrysin, DIM), MMP blockers, fat mobilizers (xanthines, forskolin, carnitine), collagen stimulators (asiatic acid, vitamin C) and compression.

Explains what peptides are, their categories (signal/matrikine, antioxidant, neuropeptide, carrier, enzyme inhibitor) and marketed cosmetic peptides such as Matrixyl, Argireline and copper GHK. Discusses delivery challenges and chemical modifications like palmitoylation and cyclization.

Describes nail unit anatomy, development, histology and composition, growth rate, and common nail pathologies. Discusses effects of nail cosmetics such as hardeners, varnishes and artificial nails on nail health.

Covers vulvar anatomy and innervation, sensory perception, and vulvar atrophy causes and physiology. Reviews OTC, estrogen and ospemifene treatments, and topical growth factors and adipose-derived stem cell secreted factors as a new cosmetic frontier.

Describes rheological parameters (viscosity, yield stress, viscoelasticity) and the main synthetic polymeric rheology modifiers: AMPS polymers, polyacrylic acid (carbomer) polymers and ASE/HASE polymers. Correlates rheology with sensory attributes (breakdown, spreadability, cushion, afterfeel) in emulsions, hydroalcoholic gels and optical-effects cleansers.

Overviews marine cosmetic resources: macroalgae, microalgae (blue algae), coastal halophyte plants and sea minerals. Presents examples for moisturization, slimming, anti-aging, oligosaccharide wound healing, exopolysaccharides, photolyase DNA repair, thioredoxin activation, retinol-like Rock Samphire and Salicornia aquaporin stimulation.
Skin's primary interface and first line of defense against pathogens and insults; barrier repair is an epigenetic study target.
Epidermal permeability barrier located in the stratum corneum, demonstrated by Blank and Scheuplein; interdependent with antimicrobial, immune, antioxidant and UV barriers.
Permeability barrier determined by stratum corneum lipids; weak on the lip vermilion.
Lipid bilayers in upper skin layers; hydrophilic surfactants can disrupt them.
Improved by HA in formulations; high-MW HA forms barrier against moisture loss.
SC permeability barrier improved by gluconolactone and lactobionic acid lowering SC pH.
Permeability higher at night; recovery rate lowest 8-11 p.m.

nodes.label: Marketing Concepts to Empower Technical People

summaries.text: Explains the marketing concept: products should be developed only when a large enough group will buy them, so development is driven by market analysis. Covers situation/SWOT analysis, market segmentation, the Four P's, the new product-development process, types of innovation, patents and the need for cross-functional cooperation, noting 80-90% of new products fail.

nodes.label: Cytokines, Growth Factors, and Stem Cells

summaries.text: Discusses intrinsic and extrinsic aging and newer cosmeceuticals: topical growth factors and cytokines (TGF-beta1, neonatal/fetal fibroblast secretions) and stem cell extracts from adipose tissue and plants such as the Uttwiler Spatlauber apple. Covers efficacy, penetration and safety concerns including VEGF and cancer.
U.S. Food and Drug Administration, increasingly watching product claims and mandating elimination of false or misleading structure-function claims.
US agency overseeing cosmetics under the FD&C Act; provides compliance guidelines, monitors the market, inspects facilities, but requires no premarket approval or registration for cosmetics.
US agency; approved hydroquinone 4% for hyperpigmentation and tretinoin for wrinkles.
US Food and Drug Administration; concluded panel hearings on antiplaque/antigingivitis agents in 1998 and published recommendations in 2003.
Food and Drug Administration established 1931; enforced 1906 law revised in 1938 to the FD&C Act adding cosmetics.
US Food and Drug Administration; approved tretinoin, adapalene and tazarotene for acne and tretinoin for photoaging.
Immune process mediated by cytokines; epigenetic changes are involved and Nrf2 signals protection against it.
Complex cellular response, acute or chronic; triggered by UV, stress, infection, impaired stratum corneum and ROS; linked to collagen/elastin breakdown and skin aging.
Response that combats infection but in excess accelerates aging and damages collagen/elastin; triggered by smoke, UV, pollution, stress, poor sleep.

nodes.label: Classification Scale for Skin Complexions Around the World

summaries.text: Argues that the 1975 Fitzpatrick scale fails to predict skin type and precautions across races and proposes the EP Global Skin Classification Scale (classes I-XI) based on race, country of origin, complexion, skin characteristics, skin type and precautions. The scale derives from a 1997-2005 San Francisco clinic study of 588 subjects using skin evaluation questionnaires, Wood's lamp and UV photography.
Unavoidable effect of time on all body sites, independent of lifestyle; reduces collagen synthesis, flattens the dermal-epidermal junction; both collagen and elastin decrease.
Chronological aging driven by genetics and hormones; in hair it causes graying from lower melanin production and androgenic hair loss.
Chronological aging from genetics, characterized by atrophic pale skin with fine wrinkles; mimicked in vitro by replicative senescence.
Internally determined, genetically programmed component of aging, one of the additive influences on skin aging.

Outermost horny layer of 10-15 layers of anucleate corneocytes in an intercellular lipid matrix (about 10 micrometers); replaced in about 14 days; constitutes 10% of skin but over 80% of barrier function.
Outermost epidermal layer; in the lip vermilion contains ceramides, cholesterol and fatty acids like other regions.
Hydrophobic outer skin layer; hydrophobic small HA fragments theoretically penetrate it better.
Lipophilic outer skin barrier limiting peptide penetration.

Surveys surfactants: history, functions (emulsifying, cleaning, foaming, solubilizing, conditioning, dispersing, lubricating), applications in creams, shampoos, cleansers, conditioners, color cosmetics and antiperspirants, physical chemistry (surface tension, micelles, charge, foam), and chemistry of anionic, nonionic, amphoteric and cationic classes.

Reviews the seven mammalian sirtuins as NAD+-dependent deacetylases, their nuclear (SIRT1, SIRT6) and mitochondrial (SIRT3-5) biochemistry, and how UVB and ozone disrupt sirtuin expression in keratinocytes. Discusses resveratrol as a sirtuin activator and nicotinamide as a potential inhibitor for hyperproliferative skin conditions.
Ingredient class whose development was stimulated by WWII-era cosmetic advances.
Ingredients ensuring self-preservation of water-containing cosmetics used in nonsterile conditions; EU positive list in Annex V, free in US.
Needed to keep extracts germ-free but negatively perceived by consumers; glycerin carriers and flash pasteurization reduce need.
Antimicrobials that kill molds, yeasts and gram-negative flora in products, slowing degradation; must be non-interfering, non-toxic, stable, active at low concentration over wide pH.
Skin disorder associated with excessive sebum production.
Result of microbial infection by Propionibacterium acnes; Ayurvedic products tested clinically.
Condition controlled by zinc-chelated oligoalginate.
Pathogenesis involves plugged follicles, inflammation, P. acnes and excess sebum; the microcomedo is the initial lesion.
Adult acne linked to abnormal cortisol rhythm.

nodes.label: Chronobiology of the Skin: Circadian Rhythm and Clock Genes

summaries.text: Describes the SCN master clock and peripheral clock genes (CLOCK/BMAL1, PER/CRY feedback loops), the health consequences of circadian desynchronization (shift-work cancers, aging), and skin circadian rhythms: daytime protection versus nighttime repair, proliferation and higher permeability. UVB downregulates skin clock genes and ATP rhythms, suggesting night-targeted anti-aging treatments.
Variable appendage producing terminal, vellus or lanugo hair; hair color from melanosomes of bulb melanocytes; accounts for 1-2% of skin surface and a penetration route.
Small organ that produces and assembles hair cells into a fiber; one per hair, 80,000-150,000 on the scalp, regenerating cyclically.
Coconut water may support growth of hair follicles; anagen phase induced by Eclipta alba.
Skin appendage cycling through anagen, catagen and telogen; Dicer deletion yields hypoproliferative follicles without hair shafts.
Anagen bulb shows high telomerase activity; bulge quiescent stem cells low.

Complex, balanced mixture of natural and synthetic odorous materials (plus ~5-20% carrier) that covers base malodor, makes products appealing and reinforces product benefits; used in nearly every product type.
Perfume and aromatic formulations; perceived scent arises from combined sensory profiles of many ingredients.
Damage ECM and skin cells; generated via pro-inflammatory interleukins; also degrade HA.
Highly reactive molecules damaging membranes, lipids, proteins and DNA; excess is a top antagonist of skin and hair.
Unstable reactive molecules whose activity damages cells and affects cell longevity.
KSA: total <=10% at pH >=3.5; leave-on products >=3% need Arabic/English cautions including sunscreen advice; FDA lists AHAs/BHAs among frequently asked ingredients.
Hydroxy acids such as glycolic and lactic acid used in peels and anti-aging products.
Acids such as glycolic acid cited as anti-aging hair ingredients benefiting shaft and root.
Keratolytic acids clarifying skin by removing dead cells; acidic and stinging.
Process inhibited by 4-hexylresorcinol.
Glucose molecules react with proteins including collagen, forming AGEs that contribute to elasticity loss, wrinkles, inflammation and accelerated aging.
Sebaceous lipid: triglycerides 57.5%, wax esters 26%, squalene 12%, free fatty acids 10%, minor cholesterol; thermoregulatory, antimicrobial; excess associated with acne.
Lipid secretion of sebaceous glands that hydrates the scalp and coats hair with a protective microfilm.
Lipid secretion composed of 57% triglycerides, 25% wax monoesters, 15% squalene, 2% cholesterol esters and 1% cholesterol; secretion decreases with age.
Skin surface oil whose overproduction gives shine; absorbed by silicone elastomers and some marine EPS.
Production highest during the day, contributing to moisturization.
Longevity-associated proteins; activating/modulating sirtuins is presented as an expanding anti-aging strategy boosting cell longevity.
Twenty building blocks of proteins classified by side-chain polarity; arginine, lysine, aspartate and glutamate dominate protein charge.
Building blocks of peptides and proteins; peptides break down into natural amino acids, conferring safety.
Vitamin C; cofactor required in collagen biosynthesis.
Antioxidant abundant in amla and other Ayurvedic botanicals.
Most popular Japanese whitening ingredient; antioxidant blocking DOPA to dopaquinone; also stimulates collagen production threefold and is critical to collagen cross-linking.
Vitamin C protectant comparable to gluconolactone in reducing UV elastin promoter activation.
Vitamin C optimizes Tet enzymes removing DNA methyl groups in embryonic stem cells.

Describes eyelash anatomy, glands and the short lash growth cycle, then the history and safety of lash conditioners, notably the prostaglandin analogue dechloro ethylcloprostenolamide. Reports clinical study results and newer peptide and adipose stem-cell-derived conditioners.

nodes.label: Ingredients for Creating the Next Greatest Lipstick

summaries.text: Explains lipstick as a crystalline wax-oil stick and the conflicting attributes of comfort, shine and long wear. Reviews traditional waxes, esters and castor oil, then new technologies: sugar esters, novel plant and silicone waxes, alkyl and phenyl silicones, elastomers, film formers, rainforest ingredients, powder fillers, effect pigments and colorants.

Covers natural versus naturally derived actives, extraction techniques (solvent, freeze-drying, supercritical CO2), and standardization of botanical extracts. Profiles multifunctional botanicals (amla, ellagic acid, tetrahydrocurcuminoids, coconut water, Coleus forskohlii, tetrahydropiperine, oxyresveratrol, Eclipta alba, ursolic acid, boswellic acids) with assay and clinical data, and botanical sustainability.

EU cosmetics law applicable since July 11, 2013, replacing Directive 76/768/EEC; requires CPNP notification, a Responsible Person, a Product Information File with safety report, GMP per ISO 22716, and defines nanomaterials.
Mesenchyme-derived principal dermal cell that secretes collagen, procollagen and other matrix constituents.
HA fragments support fibroblast proliferation.
Dermal collagen-producing cell; senescent fibroblasts enlarge and produce less collagen; in cellulite, fibroblasts secrete MMP-1 under estrogen.
Dermal cells secreting ECM; microRNAs regulate their senescence and ECM synthesis.
Cells with limited life span; embryonic fibroblasts divide ~50 times, adult ones ~20 times.
Neural crest-derived dendritic cell in the basal layer that produces melanosomes; each serves about 36-40 keratinocytes (epidermal melanin unit); number is the same regardless of skin color.
Dendritic pigment cells in the follicle bulb that synthesize melanin and transfer it into cortical keratinocytes.
Melanin-producing skin cell.
Pigment cell producing melanin in melanosomes and distributing it via dendrites to up to fifty keratinocytes.
Synthesizes melanin in melanosomes transferred to keratinocytes forming a supranuclear cap protecting DNA from UV.
Formation of melanin: tyrosine oxidized to DOPA, dehydrogenated to DOPAquinone, then eumelanin via indole-5,6-quinone or pheomelanin via cysteinyldopa; depends on free radical generation.
Biochemical pathway in melanocytes producing melanin in melanosomes with tyrosinase as the rate-limiting enzyme; ceases during catagen.
Melanin synthesis catalyzed by tyrosinase (tyrosine to DOPA to DOPA-quinone); stimulated by α-MSH via cAMP-MITF.
Melanin synthesis from L-tyrosine via L-DOPA and dopaquinone, catalyzed by tyrosinase in melanosomes.
Melanin synthesis regulated by melanogenic enzymes and transcriptional pathways potentially subject to microRNA silencing.
Vitamin A derivatives; Asian skin classes may react or be sensitive to retinoids.
Vitamin A derivatives whose benefits Rock Samphire mimics without irritation and photosensitivity.
Natural or synthetic derivatives of vitamin A used topically or orally in dermatology to treat acne, psoriasis, pigmentary disorders and photo-aging; main side effect is irritation.

Somatically heritable states of gene expression resulting from changes in chromatin structure without altering DNA sequence; influenced by environmental factors and involved in inflammation, obesity, aging, immune disorders and cancer.
Mechanisms such as DNA methylation that may elucidate aging, photoaging and skin disease; emerging in product development.
Red rice extracts suggest influence on epigenetic factors of aging via CpG promoter sequences.
Regulation of gene expression including DNA methylation, histone modification and RNA-mediated silencing.
Science challenging the assumption that aging is unstoppable deterioration; genomics increasingly used by skin care industry.

Under EU Regulation 1223/2009, insoluble or biopersistent, intentionally manufactured materials with one or more external dimensions or internal structure on the 1-100 nm scale; subject of evolving global legislation.

Stress-sensing transcription factor and master cytoprotective regulator activating >200 genes for detoxification and protection against oxidative stress and inflammation; interacts with p53 and NF-kB.
Transcription factor driving ARE-mediated phase 2 detoxifying enzymes; activated by verbascoside and chlorogenic acid.
Transcription factor controlling endogenous antioxidants and phase II enzymes; downregulated with age; upregulated by some cosmetic ingredients and sulforaphane.

nodes.label: TR CU 009/2011 Safety of Perfumery and Cosmetic Products

summaries.text: CU technical regulation approved 23.09.2011 (Decree 799), in force July 1, 2012; requires either State Registration or Declaration of Conformity, with composition, physicochemical, microbiological, toxicological and clinical parameters.
Products of glucose binding to proteins such as collagen; contribute to loss of elasticity, wrinkles, inflammation, accelerated aging.
Anti-sunburn lipsticks were among the WWII military developments that stimulated cosmetic technology.
Lip product; lip care products range from moisturizers to lipstick.
Crystalline solid of waxes, oils and colorants molded into a swivel cartridge; ~2000 shade names across 50+ US brands; sales up ~15% in 2011; melt point should be 65-75°C.
Anhydrous stick in which pigments must stay suspended while molten; benefits from suspending agents and polyethylenes.
Acquired patchy facial hyperpigmentation common in EP classes V-X.
Localized irregular hyperpigmentation treated with tranexamic acid.
Hyperpigmentation disorder best managed by combination hydroquinone, tretinoin and topical steroid therapy.

Reviews vitamin A-derived topical retinoids: their pharmacology via nuclear RAR/RXR receptors, indications (acne, melasma/PIH, photo-aging) and adverse effects. Covers OTC retinol cosmeceuticals versus prescription tretinoin, adapalene and tazarotene.

Argues that loss of intracellular water is the final common pathway of aging and disease. Reviews definitions and classifications of aging theories, Nagy's membrane hypothesis, and clinical bioelectrical impedance data showing dietary supplementation raised intracellular water, phase angle and BMR.
Small RNAs regulating genes such as p63 in proliferating and differentiating keratinocytes.
Small double-stranded noncoding RNAs of 20-25 nucleotides that bind the 3'UTR of target mRNAs causing translational repression or degradation; may target 30-60% of human transcripts.
Rinse-off micellar product; fragrance is most concentrated in bottle and on hands, then dilutes below detection thresholds as water is added.
Cleansing product; mild moisturizing shampoos recommended, avoiding harsh surfactants like SLS; silicone 2-in-1 shampoos let hair dry into its natural shape.
Typically anionic sulfate (6-12%) plus amphoteric/betaine (~5%) plus nonionic amide (~2%) plus salt for viscosity; sulfate-free poses challenges.
Surfactant cleansing product that is difficult to thicken; uses carbomer, gums, salt and other rheology modifiers.
Hair cleanser; example formulas with acyl glutamates, lauroyl lysine and zinc PCA.
Organosilicones, a polymer family listed among the editor's areas of expertise; silicones also mentioned as product bases with which fragrance carriers must be compatible.
Well-established hair care ingredients for shine; reduce inter-fiber friction so hair recovers permanent shape.
Touch modifiers of consumer concern; plant mono-esters proposed as substitutes.
Growing integral class of cosmetic ingredients offering characteristics unavailable from conventional ingredients.

Polymers containing Si-O-Si bonds, ranging from silanes and polydimethylsiloxanes to organosilicone copolymers and cross-linked gels; insoluble in water and oil with very low surface tension; major in personal care since the 1990s.

nodes.label: The Nose: Biology of Human Olfaction

summaries.text: Reviews odorant receptor biology and cell-based high-throughput screening (HTS) for discovering new all-natural fragrance ingredients. Describes fragrance enhancers and blockers, natural substitutes, and the advance of expressing native full-length odorant receptors in lab cells.
Natural fragrance materials usually obtained by steam distillation (citrus by peel expression); used at ~1-20% in standard fragrances, adding naturalness and complexity but cost volatility.
Fixed ratio of thymol, menthol, methyl salicylate and eucalyptol clinically shown to reduce gingivitis and oral malodor.
Investigated actives for improving compromised elderly skin.
Small-molecular-weight peptides used as anti-aging hair ingredients; bioactive peptides also used in second-generation lash conditioners.
Topical peptides play a role in reversing skin aging; mass-produced from adult stem cell growth media.
Recombinant peptides: tetrapeptides repress MMP-1, others inhibit tyrosinase, tripeptides influence TGF-β.

Chains of at least two amino acids joined by peptide (amide) bonds; active at very low concentrations, with bioactivity determined by sequence; popular anti-aging cosmeceuticals since the early 1990s.
Ingredients that modify flow characteristics of a fluid and add functions such as suspension, emulsion stabilization, lubricity, and stability to shear, heat, pH and freeze/thaw.
Elastic fiber protein, 4% of dermal dry weight, containing the unique amino acid desmosine; provides resilience.
ECM protein broken down by inflammation; protected by curcuminoids.
ECM protein of the dermal supporting matrix; source of matrikines.
Elastic fibers degenerate with age and are replaced by less flexible collagen; damaged by inflammation-generated free radicals.
Alpha hydroxy acid; 30-70% glycolic acid peels common for melasma; increases SC turnover.
Alpha hydroxy acid (DuPont Glypure) that penetrates the hair shaft, conditioning, moisturizing, strengthening and preventing breakage, and exfoliates the scalp to reduce flaking.
Smallest AHA (2-hydroxyethanoic acid, ~76 Da, pKa 3.8) from sugar cane; 8% cream (pH 3.8) improved crepey photodamaged skin in 15/16 studies and stimulates collagen synthesis.
Molecule toxic when it builds up in cells; H2O2-induced premature senescence of keratinocytes was prevented by AMPK activation with resveratrol.
Dental bleaching agent; products at 0.1-6.0% H2O2 (incl. from carbamide/zinc peroxide) require CU State Registration.
H2O2; accumulates at millimolar levels in gray hair shafts causing oxidative stress; used at 3% to reoxidize disulfide bonds in perms and in permanent hair color.
Peroxide bleaching agent used to reduce extrinsic or intrinsic dental stain.
Used to simulate oxidative stress inducing senescence and telomere shortening; trace levels showed hormesis-like slowing of telomere shortening.
Pigment derived from tyrosine formed in melanosomes; major determinant of skin color; a stable free radical; barrier to UV radiation.
Polymeric pigment granules (~0.8 µm) built from DHI and DHICA that color hair and act as free radical scavengers, antioxidants and UV, heat and gamma-ray absorbers.
Skin pigment reduced by ellagic acid in basal, spinous, granular and corneum layers.
Pigment synthesized in melanocytes (eumelanin and pheomelanin) and transferred to keratinocytes as a UV 'cap'.
Pigment produced in melanosomes that protects genomic DNA from UV.
Eco-sustainable approach to producing cosmetic ingredients, chapter by Roberto Dal Toso of IRB SpA.
Meristem/callus cultures producing high-value compounds sustainably (carotenoids, flavonoids) without field-grown biomass, pesticides or herbicides.
Functional cosmetic category in Japan requiring MHLW premarket approval; skin-lightening quasi-drugs prevent/improve melasma and chloasma.
MHLW category under the Pharmaceutical Affairs Law for approved actives at set doses (JSQI); whitening QD approval takes at least five years and up to 5 million dollars.
Retinoic acid and salts; not permitted at any concentration in KSA cosmetics.
Retinoid metabolized by CYP26b1 in keratinocytes; increased levels disrupt embryonic barrier formation.
All-trans retinoic acid; added to hydroquinone to enhance efficacy against hyperpigmentation.
All-trans retinoic acid (ATRA), the first topical retinoid, marketed in the 1970s as Retin-A for acne; FDA-approved for fine wrinkles, mottled hyperpigmentation and roughness of photoaged skin.
All-trans RA: master epigenetic regulator of gene transcription.

Describes fine-fragrance development as an integrated multi-sensory process aligning marketer, perfumer and designer via briefs. Uses consumer testing (e.g. Victoria's Secret Bombshell), color, bottle touch/ergonomics and storytelling as sensory cues so that packaging and scent avoid sensory dissonance.
Topical growth factors and peptides help reverse skin aging though mainly used in wound healing; include TGF-beta1, PDGF, KGF, bFGF, HGF, VEGF.
Wound-healing proteins secreted by fibroblasts, keratinocytes and melanocytes that increase fibroblast/keratinocyte proliferation and ECM; large hydrophilic molecules with limited penetration.
Polyphenol associated with Nrf2 activation that activates AMPK and prevented H2O2-induced premature senescence in human keratinocyte cultures.
Natural alternative to hydroquinone for hyperpigmentation.
Polyphenol produced by small-molecule fermentation, bridging nutrition and personal care.
Polyphenolic stilbene from red wine/Polygonum cuspidatum; SIRT1 activator extending yeast lifespan 70%; up-regulates glutathione enzymes; not photostable.
Found capable of counteracting immunosenescence leading to cellular rejuvenation.

nodes.label: Regulatory Requirements, IP and Global Market Success

summaries.text: Co-editors' introduction to Part 2, covering the nontechnical knowledge needed for global product success: changing regulations, market access by region, and patenting. Highlights ICCR harmonization topics, especially alternatives to animal testing and nanomaterials.

nodes.label: Green and Sustainable Bioactives from Biofermentation

summaries.text: Describes fermentation and cell culture (submerged and solid-state) as sustainable means of producing cosmetic bioactives from yeast, Lactobacillus, fungi, algae and plant meristem cultures. Covers environmental advantages over chemical synthesis and activities such as live yeast cell derivatives, algal MMP and tyrosinase inhibitors, plant stem cell extracts, flavonoids and recombinant peptides and hyaluronic acid.
U.S. patents require novelty, a non-obvious inventive step and industrial application and are exclusive for 20 years; author argues cosmetic patents are too easy to obtain.
Territorial exclusive right granted for disclosure, generally 20 years from filing; claims define coverage; requires novelty, nonobviousness and utility.
Vitamin A; with esters retinyl acetate and palmitate permitted at <=1% in KSA cosmetics.
Vitamin A; produces tretinoin-like changes, much less effective but less irritating; 0.15% improves wrinkling and hyperpigmentation in 12 weeks; can be unstable.
Main OTC vitamin A derivative and 'original cosmeceutical', typically used at 1-2% though benefits seen at 0.1%; less irritating but less effective than prescription retinoids.
Vitamin A; retinoid signaling crosstalks with epigenetic factors; all-trans retinoic acid is a master epigenetic regulator.
Passive diffusion of actives through the stratum corneum; only molecules under 500 Da penetrate; depends on skin condition, site, hydration, molecular size and vehicle.
HA >500 kDa does not penetrate and forms barrier films; smaller fragments permeate; permeability inversely related to size.
Peptide permeability depends on pKa, molecular size, binding affinity, solubility and partition coefficient; a key formulation challenge.
Phyllanthus emblica; among richest vitamin C sources, high tannins; actives gallic and ellagic acid; mitigates UVA/UVB photodamage.

Describes the structure and physicochemical properties of hyaluronan, preparation and characterization of HA fragments and chemical derivatives, skin penetration as a function of molecular weight, and molecular-weight-dependent moisturizing and anti-aging effects in cosmetics.

Explains lipid auto-oxidation (initiation by heat, light, metals and enzymes; propagation; termination into odorous carbonyls) as a main cause of reduced cosmetic shelf life. Classifies primary antioxidants (BHT, BHA, TBHQ, tocopherols, rosemary extract) and secondary antioxidants (chelators, ascorbic acid, carotenoids), and reviews assays (OSI, peroxide value, secondary products) and the polar paradox.
Keratin fiber produced by the follicle; an optimized assembly of proteins, lipids and polysaccharides whose mature cells are dead but whose proteins retain biological activity.
Dihydroxybenzene; prohibited in KSA cosmetics; hydroquinone skin-whitening products excluded from cosmetics.
Skin-lightening agent; Asian and mixed skin classes may react to it, requiring caution.
Potent melanin inhibitor but toxic, use restricted; 4% caused adverse reactions in 50% of subjects.
Parent phenol of arbutin.
Skin-bleaching agent combined with tretinoin (which enhances its penetration) and a steroid for melasma.

Chronic immune/genetic inflammatory disease with abnormally rapid transformation of basal cells into horny cells, scaling plaques, T-cell and neutrophil infiltration; treated with anti-TNF, anti-IL-12/23.
Inflammatory skin disease that increases nail growth rate and causes pitting, onycholysis and yellow discoloration of nails.
Condition in which defensins are overproduced, so topical probiotics may be unsuitable.
Skin condition among retinoid indications.
Hyperproliferative skin condition potentially improved by sirtuin inhibitors.
Elastomer particles in silicone carrier gels or powders; excellent film formers, first used medically; range of viscosities and tack.

Lightly cross-linked dimethicone polymers (dimethicone crosspolymers, Polysilicone-11) forming 3D swellable networks of 5-50 micron particles; provide silky texture, mattifying, line filling, sebum absorption and controlled release.
Water diffusing/evaporating from the body through the epidermis; increased by barrier disruption (wounds, solvents, surfactants); a key measure in skin care development.
Water loss through skin; higher through the lip vermilion than the cheek and decreases with age.
Lowered by high-MW HA films on upper epidermis.
Water loss through the skin reduced by high-MW marine polysaccharide films and Salicornia treatment.
Reduced by amino acid-derived emollients, increasing hydration.
About 25% higher at night than morning/afternoon, reflecting higher barrier permeability.
Slower with age; main use of growth factors; ADSC secretory factors promote it.
Accelerated by S. cerevisiae lysates.
Epidermal recovery from wounds accelerated by alginate oligosaccharides.
Tissue repair process stimulated by matrikines, copper peptides and RGD peptides.
Delayed by stress-elevated epinephrine; beta-blockers improve burn re-epithelialization.

Editor's preface tracing Harry's Cosmeticology from Ralph Gordon Harry's 1954 first edition to the 9th edition, and the WWII military origins of modern cosmetics (sunscreens, flashburn creams, anti-sunburn lipsticks). It argues that population aging, genetics and epigenetics place the industry at a tipping point in the search for youth.
Reviews the vermilion zone of the lip, its weak barrier and high TEWL, sebaceous follicles and sebum composition, stratum corneum ceramides, and age-related changes in lip morphology.

Introduces Ayurveda, the ancient Indian holistic medicine system based on doshas and plant ingredients, and its relevance to green personal care. Reviews Ayurvedic botanicals with antioxidant (amla), anti-inflammatory (turmeric/curcumin) and antimicrobial (neem, triphala) benefits.

Covers the history of cosmetic preservation since the 1938 FD&C Act, frequency of preservative use in the US and Canada, banned preservatives, and six factors encouraging microbial growth (water activity, nutrients, pH, osmotic pressure, surface tension, temperature). Lists preservative selection criteria and frames product success with a four-quadrant model.
Covalent S-S bond formed by oxidation of two cysteine sulfhydryls, common in extracellular proteins to maintain folded structure.
Covalent cystine cross-link stabilizing the hair amorphous matrix and keratin structure; its scission underlies perms, relaxers and heat damage.
Nuclear factor kappa B, a key cell regulator interacting with Nrf2 in age-related disease.
Inflammatory transcription factor pathway inhibited by verbascoside and chlorogenic acid.
Key inflammatory mediator modulated by curcuminoids.
Transcription factor activated after UVA by iron release; inhibited by bakuchiol.
Inflammatory transcription factor; stimulated by AGEs; buildup in rheumatoid arthritis.
Pigment increase after inflammation such as acne; prominent in Asian, Mediterranean and African skin classes.
Pigmentary disorder for which retinoids are adjunctive treatment with bleaching agents.
Major stratum corneum intercellular lipid class; generated from glucosylceramides; covalently bound to corneocyte envelopes; requires very-long-chain fatty acids (ELOVL4).
Lipid of the cuticle and CMC (with fatty acids and cholesterol) and an anti-aging hair ingredient.
Fatty acid amide-linked to a long-chain base; all nine structural types found in lip stratum corneum, e.g. NP 23.3%, NH 20.9%, AH 17.4%, EOS 4.4%.
Skin lipids increased in keratinocytes by liposomal ursolic acid.
Type 3 ceramide compared to glutamate emollients in barrier recovery; ceramides leach from damaged hair.

nodes.label: Ingredients to Strengthen Skin Barrier Integrity

summaries.text: Reviews epidermal barrier organization (keratinocyte differentiation, cytokeratins, desmosomes, tight junctions, dermal-epidermal junction, filaggrin) and the role of calcium signaling, which declines with aging. Presents a hydrophilic extract of the brown alga Padina pavonica that mobilizes calcium, stimulating cytokeratin and desmosome synthesis, restoring cell communication and protecting against pollutants.
Dyes regulated by positive list in US (21 CFR 73/74, FDA approval; batch-certified or exempt) and EU (Annex IV, identified by colour index).
Colorants depositing color; some (D&C Red 6/7 lakes, yellow iron oxide) have high oil absorbance; ground in castor oil via ball or three-roll mill.
Plant-derived compound reported to activate AMPK.
Curcuminoid secondary metabolite of turmeric; modulates TNFα, NFκB, COX2, IL1; protects collagen and elastin; antioxidant and may suppress cancers.
Turmeric pigment inhibiting DNMT1, HDACs, HATs, miRNAs; HDAC inhibition more potent than valproic acid; restores HDAC2.
Tooth decay from demineralization by acids produced by plaque bacteria fermenting carbohydrates; early white-spot lesions can be reversed by remineralization.
Shedding of corneocytes from the skin surface, in equilibrium with basal mitosis; enabled by protease degradation of corneodesmosomes.
Shedding of corneocytes after enzymatic breakdown of corneodesmosomes.
Shedding of corneocytes; accelerating it removes melanin from skin surface.
Shedding of corneocytes; AHAs enhance it possibly via pH activation of acid proteases such as kallikreins and cathepsin D.
Addition of a methyl group to cytosine (or adenine) that alters gene expression; promoters become hypermethylated with age and it plays a role in sun-exposed aging skin.
Addition of methyl groups to cytosine at CpG sites by DNMTs using SAM, silencing genes; with age CpG islands become hypermethylated and non-island sites globally hypomethylated.
Eleven-class skin classification by Eva Patel (2012) covering race, country of origin, complexion, skin characteristics, skin type and precautions, designed to fill gaps of the Fitzpatrick scale.
Female sex hormone; inhibits sebaceous secretion in humans.
Hormone with profound effect on vulvar touch sensitivity; topical low-dose estrogen is first-line pharmacologic treatment for vulvar atrophy, accelerating healing and decreasing inflammation.
Ovarian steroid (17β-estradiol) that stimulates fibroblasts to secrete MMP-1; body fat is the second largest estrogen producer even at menopause.
Dermal matrix whose renewal is a skin-care target of epigenetic studies.
HA is a main ECM component in connective, epithelial and neural tissues; high-MW HA contributes to its structure.
Network of proteins (collagens, laminin, fibronectin, elastin, proteoglycans) anchoring cells and mediating receptor-induced signaling.
Biotransformation of simple nutrients (sugars) by organisms into secondary metabolites, vitamins, enzymes, peptides; used since 3000 BCE; sustainable route to cosmetic bioactives.
Main industrial amino acid production using screened microorganisms fed sugars, with 10-30 enzymes in sequence; enables low-cost mass production.
Family of fibrous structural proteins formed from intermediate filaments; type I acidic (K9-K20) and type II basic (K1-K8) keratins pair as dimers; key component of stratum corneum, hair and nails.

Helical structural protein providing mechanical strength; hair is rich in half-cystine, serine, glutamic acid and proline typical of keratin. Alpha (soft) keratins occur in hair, nails and skin; types I (acidic) and II (basic) are coiled in pairs.
Tough structural protein; nail keratin is hard keratin similar to hair, high in sulfur (cystine), with lower lipid content than skin keratin.
Hair protein composed of amino acids.
Alpha hydroxy acid used in combination and lactic peels; long-known moisturizer.
Reacted with fatty acids to form lactylate surfactants.
Chemical exfoliator used to accelerate epidermal turnover for whitening.
3-carbon AHA from milk, endogenous metabolite; thickens epidermis (5-12%), stimulates ceramide synthesis and VEGF secretion.
Water-soluble hygroscopic compounds, mainly free amino acids from filaggrin breakdown, representing about 10% of corneocyte mass, that hold water in the stratum corneum.
Hygroscopic substances, including HA, that buffer skin and preserve appearance.
Skin humectant mix strengthened by microalgal amino acids with sea minerals and increased by Salicornia.
Humectant mixture in corneocytes: 40% amino acids, 12% PCA, 12% lactates, 7% urea plus other components.
Unintended trace contaminants in cosmetic ingredients or products; an ICCR priority topic and a focus of safety assessment.
Chinese authority (formerly SFDA) regulating cosmetics since taking over from the Ministry of Health in 2008; requires registration and animal testing for imported cosmetics.

Describes cross-linked dimethicone elastomers as 3D swellable networks that deliver silky sensory feel, mattifying oil control, line filling, soft focus and controlled release. Discusses cross-link density, solvent exchange with cyclopentasiloxane, and example serum formulations with Polysilicone-11.
Molecular oscillatory system proposed as a candidate for the clock controlling anagen duration.
Diurnal gene expression coordinated by CLOCK/BMAL-1; SIRT1 deacetylates BMAL-1 influencing skin cell rhythms.
Daytime skin is thicker, higher pH and sebum for protection; at night higher temperature, blood flow, permeability, TEWL (~25% higher), DNA repair and 30-fold higher proliferation.

Rules on label content: US PDP and information panels with letter size rules; EU name/address of RP, nominal content, minimum durability or PAO, precautions, batch number, function and ingredient list.
Oral care active; CU State Registration needed above 0.15% (0.05% liquids) and fluoride content labeling required; makes US toothpaste a cosmetic/drug.
Decreases acid solubility of hydroxyapatite (forming fluorapatite), increases remineralization and inhibits cariogenic bacteria; used in water fluoridation, toothpastes and mouthrinses.
Alkaline (pH 11.5-14) or thio/sulfite creams that permanently straighten curly hair; the most damaging permanent reshaping treatment.
Low-MW HA oligosaccharides; 6-20 units are pro-angiogenic; <5 kDa suppress wrinkles; ≤50 kDa act as signals for new HA synthesis.
Phytochemical class including quercetin, resveratrol, caffeic acid and catechins, associated with Nrf2 activation.
Plant antioxidants (flavonoids, tannins, catechols); reduce UV skin damage; inherently unstable.
Dietary polyphenols (resveratrol, curcumin, quercetin, catechins) modulating NF-kB, MAPK and activating sirtuins.
26S barrel-shaped multi-subunit protease complex with core and two caps; activity decreases up to age 50; malfunction may contribute to skin aging.
Endpoint FDA recommends evaluating for nanomaterials, along with sensitization, phototoxicity, genotoxicity and repeat-dose toxicity.
Reactivity to irritants (SLS, soap, octanoic acid); decreases or is not more marked with age.
Cationic and anionic surfactants have the highest irritation potential.
Main side effect of topical retinoids: redness, scaling, dryness, itching, stinging and burning.
Surface-active agents (detergents) developed after WWII; in fragrance work surfactants such as polysorbates solubilize or disperse hydrophobic fragrance oils in water.
Surface active agents; amphiphilic molecules with hydrophilic polar head and hydrophobic tail that lower interfacial tension. Classified into anionic, nonionic, cationic and amphoteric by charge.
Telomeres are especially sensitive to UV damage; shortening may significantly affect photo-aging.
Progressive loss of telomeres with each cell division, leading to instability, senescence and death.
Vitamin E, among the most studied antioxidants for photo-aging protection.
Vitamin E compounds with chromanol ring and phytyl chain in four forms; activity δ > γ > β ≈ α; α-tocopherol pro-oxidant at high concentrations.
Vitamin E protectant comparable to gluconolactone.
Vitamin E forms combined with procyanidins for anti-glycation.
Adult stem cells from subcutaneous fat secreting cytokines and growth factors (paracrine effect); injection increased collagen expression 40x in pig skin and reduced UVB wrinkles.
Mesenchymal stem cells from human fat; conditioned media (ASC-CM) promote collagen, decrease MMP-1, protect against UVB oxidative stress, inhibit melanogenesis and lighten skin.

AMP-activated protein kinase, a three-protein master metabolic sensor regulating cellular energy homeostasis, lipid and glucose metabolism and mitochondrial biogenesis; intersects mTOR, ERK, p53 and ATM pathways.
Surfactants with net negative charge; used in largest volume for foaming and cleansing and as emulsifiers; skin/eye irritation potential can be high.
Marketing term not recognized by the FDA (nor by China); a product with significant physiological action is a drug or cosmetic/drug.
Cosmetic products with active, skin-altering effects; corrective cosmeceuticals for ethnic skin must address multiple conditions.
Term coined by Albert Kligman for effective ingredients between drug and cosmetic; not a regulatory category defined by FDA.
Skin layer drained by lymphatic and vascular conduits through which immune cells traffic.
Layer beneath the epidermis (0.3-3.0 mm) of protein fibers in a GAG-rich ground substance; divided into papillary and reticular layers; cushions against mechanical injury and nourishes the epidermis.
Contains most skin HA, in equilibrium with lymphatic and vascular systems; level remains constant with aging.
Loss of hair pigment with age (canities) due to decreased melanin production by follicle melanocytes; 74% of people aged 45-65 have gray hair.
Tetra-oxygenated stilbene; Artonox from Artocarpus lakoocha heartwood at 95%; tyrosinase IC50 0.049 µg/ml (140x kojic acid), 9x resveratrol; DPPH IC50 2.7; anti-inflammatory via NF-κB/COX-2.
Classified as nonmelanoma skin cancer and cutaneous malignant melanoma; one in five Americans will develop one; linked to sun exposure and tanning beds.
Most severe consequence of photo-oxidative damage.
Growth factor stimulating collagen production; fibroblast sensitivity reduced by AP-1.
TGF-b1 cytokine secreted by DHT-stimulated dermal papilla cells; promotes apoptosis and catagen, while TGF-b signals also activate stem cells at end of telogen.
Transforming growth factor in stem cell conditioned media; linked to whitening effect of ADSCs.
Influenced by tripeptides to improve skin structure.
Growth factor through which palmitoyl tripeptide drives collagen synthesis.
UV band harming mainly the epidermis via direct DNA absorption forming pyrimidine dimers (signature mutations) and indirectly via ROS; impairs Langerhans cells.
Low non-cytotoxic UVB (10 mJ/cm2) abrogates SIRT3/SIRT4 expression, lowers ATP and raises H2O2 in keratinocytes.
Acquired depigmentation affecting 0.5-1% of the population, with absence of melanocytes; likely autoimmune in genetically predisposed people; localized, generalized or universal (>=80% involvement).
A miR-196a-2 mutation (rs11614913 C allele) may decrease vitiligo risk.
Gynoid lipodystrophy: fat bulging through stretched collagen fibers giving orange-peel skin on hips, thighs, buttocks.
Gynoid lipodystrophy occurring on buttocks and thighs; fat herniates where type I collagen trabeculae are dissolved, producing an undulating surface; treatable but not curable.

Argues live organisms are not required for probiotic bioactivity and proposes the term Probiotic Derived Bioactive. Explains how microbial molecules such as beta-1,3-D-glucans, lipoteichoic acid and peptidoglycans activate toll-like receptors on keratinocytes to produce antimicrobial defensins, and how in vitro epithelial models with ELISA test efficacy.
Basement membrane zone between epidermis and dermis composed of basal cell plasma membrane, lamina lucida, basal lamina and dermal fibrils.
Basement membrane (lamina lucida with integrins, laminin 5, fibronectin; lamina densa with collagen IV) anchoring epidermis to dermis; flattens with age reducing firmness.
Four-zone interface (hemidesmosomes, lamina lucida with laminin 5, lamina densa with collagen IV, anchoring fibrils of collagen VII); flattens with loss of rete pegs in aging.
Intercellular bridge connecting keratinocytes; gives the stratum spinosum its spiny appearance; corneodesmosomes connect corneocytes (desmocollin, desmoglein).
Calcium-dependent press-stud junctions between keratinocytes anchored by cytokeratin filaments; hemi-desmosomes at DEJ, corneo-desmosomes in SC; number declines with age.
Corneocyte adhesion structure (desmocollins 3/4, desmoplakins I-III) down-regulated by Rock Samphire to promote exfoliation.
Polydimethylsiloxane silicone polymer; can fill cuticle air gaps or smooth the surface to enhance hair color and shine, and lowers inter-fiber friction.
Silicone backbone to which EO/PO are added to make silicone copolyol emulsifiers.
Linear polydimethylsiloxane (MDnM) silicone fluid, Newtonian, 1 to 1,000,000 cSt, surface tension 26.6 dynes/cm at 20 cP; used typically below 3% and forms a breathable protective film.
Kinetically stable but thermodynamically unstable dispersion of oil and water; surfactants aid droplet creation and stabilization against creaming, Ostwald ripening and coalescence.
A mixture of oil and water where one phase is suspended as tiny droplets in the other to create a stable dispersion.
O/W, W/O and W/Si emulsions; low-pH AHA emulsions are difficult to stabilize.

Histidine-rich filament-aggregating protein from keratohyalin (from profilaggrin) that aligns keratin into macrofibers; then hydrolyzed into free amino acids of NMF; mutations linked to atopic dermatitis and ichthyosis vulgaris.
Aggregates keratin filaments into macrofibrils forming keratin matrix scaffold for cornified envelope; mutation disrupts barrier, increases water loss and inflammation.
Epidermal protein whose production is increased by Salicornia extract.
Odorless solvents (~5-20% of a fragrance) needed for physical stability or as processing aids; must match the product base solubility.
Outer sheath of 5-11 stacked flat cuticle cells (~0.5 µm thick each) arranged like roof shingles that protects the cortex and controls lubricity, friction and optical properties.
Outer hair layer damaged by washing; repaired by CAE.
Cyclic follicle activity of anagen (growth), catagen (regression) and telogen (rest), plus exogen and kenogen; disturbances underlie most hair growth disorders.
Cycles of growth (anagen), regression (catagen) and rest (telogen).
Concern addressed by hair regrowth, cited as an example of a new market application constituting discontinuous innovation.
Premature hair loss and excessive shedding from interruption of the hair cycle, leading to baldness; a multibillion-dollar market.
HA oligosaccharides are components of compositions combating hair loss and stimulating hair growth.
Keratinocyte-specific microRNA, >100-fold higher in skin than other organs, forming a basal-low/suprabasal-high gradient; master regulator of epidermal differentiation, repressing stemness via DNp63.
Central theme of the focus book: defining sustainability and how it changes the innovation process in cosmetics.

Colorless hydrogenated metabolite of curcuminoids (Sabiwhite, INCI tetrahydrodiferuloylmethane); tyrosinase IC50 2.0, melanogenesis IC50 3.5; DPPH SC50 1.14 vs resveratrol 3.24; 0.25% outperformed 4% hydroquinone.
Historical basis of chemical safety testing; being phased out for cosmetics under consumer pressure and regulatory recognition of its lack of humaneness, the highest-priority regulatory topic.
Programmed cell death that removes cells with excessive DNA damage.
Programmed cell death; in hair, cells die in the follicle before beginning their functional life, and catagen is driven by apoptosis.
Programmed cell death via apoptosome and caspase-3/7 activation triggered by peroxynitrite oxidative stress.
Programmed cell death; critical in understanding aging, embryo development and immune protection against abnormal cells.
High-value compounds produced sustainably via plant-cell culture.
Lipophilic plant pigments (beta-carotene, lycopene, lutein) reacting with almost any radical; UV lowers skin lycopene 31-46%; beta-carotene supplementation linked to cancer in smokers.
Peroxisomal enzyme that breaks down hydrogen peroxide into water and oxygen.
Antioxidant enzyme breaking down H2O2 to water and oxygen; expression is reduced in unpigmented and older follicles.
Enzyme converting hydrogen peroxide to water and oxygen; significantly decreased in aged dermis.
Metal-containing antioxidant enzyme balancing oxidative stress.
Terminally differentiated, anucleate, keratin-filled keratinocyte forming the bricks of the stratum corneum; enclosed by a cross-linked cornified envelope.
Final enucleated form of keratinocyte filled with modified cytokeratins.
Surface stratum corneum cell; accelerating its desquamation removes melanin.
Cluster of specialized fibroblast-derived cells at the follicle base; the follicle 'command center' that instructs proliferation, differentiation and hair size via growth factors.
Mesenchymal stem cell reservoirs inducing skin appendage formation; protected from stress by Saberry+Cococin.
Four main mechanisms: charge (ionic), steric (nonionic), liquid crystalline lamellar phase, and polymeric stabilization; seldom used in isolation.
Resistance of an emulsion to creaming, phase separation and coalescence; rheology modifiers in the external or internal phase slow droplet movement.
Outer skin layer containing keratinocytes, Langerhans cells, T-cells and other immune cells.
Outermost skin layer, a stratified squamous epithelium 0.05-1.5 mm thick (about 100 micrometers typical), made primarily of keratinocytes; replaced about every 42 days.
HA most prominent in upper spinous and granular layers (extracellular); epidermal HA disappears in senile skin.
Aging from lifestyle choices, mainly UV photo-aging and also cigarette smoke exposure.
Environmentally driven aging from UV, pollution, smoking, diet and lifestyle that degrades hair via lipid oxidation, disulfide cleavage, amino acid and melanin degradation.
Aging due to environmental factors, mainly UV, causing hypertrophic skin, irregular pigmentation and pronounced wrinkling.

nodes.label: Federal Food, Drug, and Cosmetic Act

summaries.text: Main US law for cosmetics (adopted 1938); defines cosmetics (excluding soap) and drugs, and prohibits adulterated (Sec. 601) and misbranded (Sec. 602) cosmetics.
US law that does not recognize cosmeceuticals; a product is a drug, a cosmetic or both.
1938 revision of the 1906 Food and Drug Law that officially added cosmetics.
Study of genes, their protein products and regulatory networks; bioactive ingredients' effects can be detected via molecular assays using known markers.
Measurement of which genes are turned on/off (microarrays, qPCR) used in cosmetics to screen raw materials, show efficacy and mechanism, and assess safety.
Endogenous antioxidant controlling ROS damage.
Endogenous antioxidant balancing cellular oxidative stress; reacts with prostaglandin J2 cyclopentenone.
Acidic polysaccharides of the dermal ground substance (hyaluronic acid, chondroitin sulfate, dermatan sulfate) holding copious water.
ECM components whose synthesis is stimulated by signal peptides.
Flat or curling irons at 160-230°C that dehydrate hair, partially melt crystalline keratin and soften the amorphous matrix above Tm/Tg, locking shapes by vitrification on cooling; causes damage.
Large raised abnormal scar; tendency noted in Asian III, Pacific Islander and Black skin classes.
Scar tissue overgrowth from abnormal wound healing with fibroblast proliferation and collagen overproduction; differential microRNAs including up-regulated miR-21.
Non-FDA-approved natural alternative to hydroquinone for hyperpigmentation; used in combination peels for melasma.
Benchmark skin lightener; tyrosinase IC50 3.0, melanogenesis IC50 100 µg/ml in comparisons.
Copper-chelating tyrosinase inhibitor, QD in 1988 at 1%; clinically tested on freckles and age spots; discouraged by MHLW in 2003 over carcinogenicity concerns.
Skin lightener outperformed by hexylresorcinol.
Immune cell present in the epidermis contributing to skin immune homeostasis.
Epidermal resident dendritic antigen-presenting cell (3-5% of suprabasal cells) with Birbeck granules; captures antigens via langerin; impaired by UVB and decreases with age.
Skin immune cells bearing toll-like receptors.
Surfactants with no charge, first developed in the 1930s by Atlas Powder Company (sorbitan esters); best solubilizers; used for steric stabilization.
Holocrine gland, usually attached to hair follicles, densest on scalp, face, chest (400-900/cm2); androgen-stimulated; cell division to rupture takes about 14 days.
Gland releasing sebum in concert with the follicle (pilosebaceous unit) to maintain the hair shaft; sebum output decreases with age.
Sirtuin deacetylase regulating cell growth and apoptosis via p53; target of miR-34a.
Nuclear sirtuin deacetylating histones for gene silencing, deacetylating BMAL-1, activating p53, attenuating FOXO; promotes keratinocyte differentiation.
Skin with enough pigment to impart a color other than white (African, Asian, Latin, Native American, Pacific Islander, mixed origin); global skin color landscape shifting toward darker tones.
Growth phase of the follicle (2-6 years on scalp, 1-4 months for eyelashes) with intense matrix cell proliferation.
Active growth phase of hair follicles, induced by Eclipta alba.
Most common patterned hair loss: androgen-driven miniaturization of genetically predisposed follicles with shortened anagen and more telogen/kenogen.
Male pattern baldness with up-regulated miR-221, miR-125b, miR-106b and miR-410.
Itchy chronic skin inflammation with barrier dysfunction; associated with filaggrin mutations and unique gene expression profiles.
Dry, flaky, itchy skin in which all standard amino acids in skin are significantly reduced.
Cross-linked polyacrylic acid polymer that builds pseudoplastic viscosity, forms clear gels and stabilizes emulsions; salt sensitivity allows lotions to break down quickly on skin.

Section overview introducing anti-aging research from genomics to apoptosis. Highlights sirtuins, stem cells, DNA repair, glycation/AGEs, telomere theory, beauty from within, sleep, senescence and epigenetics.
Short (4-14 mm) curved hairs on the eyelids, 300-400 on the upper and 100-150 on the lower lid, with a short anagen phase.
Melanocyte organelle in which tyrosinase forms melanin; number and size, not melanocyte count, determine skin color.
Cytoplasmic organelle where hair melanins form; transferred via dendrites to cortex and medulla keratinocytes.
Organelle in which melanin is made and transported to dendrites; regulated by OA1, MART1, MLPH genes.
Melanocyte organelle where melanin is synthesized and transferred to keratinocytes.

Hydrophilic fraction of Padina (HFP) from brown alga farmed in Malta; mobilizes keratinocyte calcium, raising cytokeratin synthesis ~85% at 50 µg/ml and desmosome expression dose-dependently; protects against sulfuric acid and nicotine.

Evaluation by a qualified expert of ingredient toxicology, exposure and finished-product tests to conclude a product is safe under normal and foreseeable use; voluntary in US (else warning), compulsory in EU PIF.
2012 guideline classifying drugs, herbal, health and cosmetic products; adds bans (tretinoin, hydroquinone, triclosan) and limits (retinol 1%, sulfur 2%, urea 10%, AHAs 10%).
Viscoelastic property; extensibility (Uf) and elastic recovery (Ur/Uf) decrease with age, Ur/Uf most strongly (R2=0.656).
Decreases with declining HA production during aging.
Measured as elongation to break on Fudo rheometer; increased by sodium PCA and polyaspartate.
Angiogenic factor up-regulated by UVB in keratinocytes, endothelial cells and fibroblasts.
VEGF, potent angiogenic factor produced by ORS keratinocytes, upregulated with perifollicular vascularization during anagen.
Vascular endothelial growth factor promoting new blood vessel formation; in ADSC conditioned media.
Vascular growth factor whose secretion is increased by 1.5-3% lactic acid, possibly explaining AHA microvascular effects.
Amino acid positively charged at neutral pH, a major contributor to protein charge.
Amino acid nitric oxide precursor (Ajinomoto) reported to stimulate hair regrowth and strengthen hair by nourishing roots.
Used with calcium carbonate in dentifrices to block open dentinal tubules.
Alkaline amino acid that raises pH of AHA/BHA products without reducing efficacy, smooths hair and neutralizes gel polymers.
Circadian heterodimer; CLOCK acetyltransferase acetylates BMAL-1; limited by SIRT1 deacetylation.
Signaling molecules regulating growth, differentiation, migration, immunity and inflammation; malfunction leads to arthritis, cardiac disease and cancer.
