Small signaling proteins/glycoproteins from keratinocytes, LCs, macrophages, fibroblasts, lymphocytes (interleukins, interferons, TNF, CSFs, growth factors); production rises upon challenge.
Immune-regulating secreted factors also involved in skin repair; combined with growth factors in topical products.
Xerosis common in the elderly, prone to itching, with distinctive line patterns on legs; multifactorial (lower PCA, slower SC renewal, less lactate and glycerol).
Dehydration addressed by marine polysaccharides and Salicornia.
Excessive skin dryness linked to hyperosmolarity and senescence; target of osmoprotective agents.
Natural alternative to hydroquinone for hyperpigmentation.
Primary active component of amla.
Polyphenol from oak galls, berries, pomegranates and walnuts; copper chelator; QD for Lion in 1996 at 0.5%.
Product containing ammonia at levels whose odor fragrance can only slightly mitigate.
Hair colorants requiring CU State Registration; special-use in China; exempted from some US adulteration rules.
Permanent and demi-permanent dyes used to cover gray; permanent color oxidizes proteins and lipids via ammonia and H2O2.
International Nomenclature of Cosmetic Ingredients names listed by the PCPC, used for ingredient labels; INCI fragrance blends list each material instead of 'fragrance'.
Conventional worldwide naming system for cosmetic ingredient labeling; presence of an INCI name does not authorize an ingredient, nor does absence prohibit it.
Interstitial collagenase secreted by fibroblasts under estrogen/progesterone and IL-1alpha control; dissolves type I collagen trabeculae in cellulite.

Neutral amino sugar (NAG), component of GAGs, chitin and hyaluronic acid; 8% cream raised skin thickness 16.2% and pinch recoil 12.2%, inhibits tyrosinase glycosylation and synergizes with retinoic acid on HA (2.5-fold).
Vitamin B3 amide; listed as alternative to hydroquinone for hyperpigmentation.
Used as hydroxycitrate (2.2%) and salicylate (4.0%) in the anti-aging cream.
Airway collapse during sleep causing oxygen desaturation, HPA activation, fragmented sleep; graded by AHI; increases oxidative stress, reduces growth hormone; more prevalent with age.
Tumor suppressor protein encoded by TP53, 'guardian of the genome', regulating the cell cycle; interacts with Nrf2 and AMPK.
Apoptosis-inducing protein rapidly degraded by increased proteasome activity; link to cancer caveat.

Dimethicone copolyols: silicones with pendant PEG/PPG chains giving amphiphilic surfactant behavior (wetting at ~500 Da, emulsification ~2,500, conditioning ~10,000, waterproofing ~50,000); the term 'silicone copolyol' is obsolete.
Alignment of cosmetic regulations across countries; harmonized guidelines streamline assessment, reduce development time and duplication, and minimize in vivo testing without compromising safety.
Moisture state of skin, a target of gene expression and epigenetic studies.
Upper lip hydration greater than lower; submucosa less hydrated than rest of vermilion.
In a 60-day study with 0.005% HA, 4.6 and 17 kDa fragments raised hydration first month; 1.66 MDa HA best after three months.
Key to youthful appearance; correlates linearly with SC amino acid content.
Surfactant irritant; older skin shows lower reactivity to SLS.
Harsh surfactant to avoid in daily cleansing because it strips natural oils.
Toothpaste surfactant suggested as a predisposing factor for canker sores.
Typical sulfate anionic surfactant used in shampoos and body washes.
Anionic fatty surfactant reducing water surface tension from 72 to ~30 dynes/cm; co-surfactant in RF50 studies.
Irritant (SLS) used to challenge skin barrier.
Immature precursor cells capable of self-renewal and multi-lineage differentiation; adult stem cells have fewer ethical and control issues than embryonic.
Cells that self-renew and differentiate; their extracts contain growth factors and cytokines used in serums and creams.
Stem-cell-ness correlates with telomere length; telomere loss may contribute to stem cell dysfunction.
Antioxidant enzyme in ADSC conditioned media protecting skin from oxidative damage.
Most important endogenous enzyme for mitigating reactive oxygen.
Endogenous antioxidant enzyme; large protein that cannot penetrate cell membranes.
Major metal-containing antioxidant enzyme; activity reduced by free radical damage.
A measure of the resistance of a fluid to deformation or flow; higher viscosity contributes to emulsion stability and is associated with luxuriousness.
Alkyl-modified silicones soluble in oils and petrolatum, insoluble in dimethicone; hardness/melt point rise with alkyl length (C32+ melt ≥60°C).
Amphiphilic silicones with silicone- and oil-soluble groups that lower oil surface tension (soybean oil 32 to 22 dynes/cm), improve spread and gel oils; C16 or less liquid, C18+ solid.
Skin's interlinked defense of enzymes and non-enzymatic antioxidants maintaining pro-oxidant/antioxidant balance; can be overwhelmed by exogenous ROS.
Adding a chelating agent and keeping the product slightly acidic can help prevent fragrance-induced color change.
Bind metal ions neutralizing their ability to initiate oxidation; important in high water activity O/W emulsions, soaps, shampoos.
Major market where imported cosmetics require CFDA registration and animal testing; announced removal of mandatory animal tests for domestic non-special-use cosmetics from June 2014.
Skin care market over 35 billion yuan (US$5.5 billion), of which whitening products are 71%.
May exceed 10% in KSA bath preparations meant to be diluted.
Acid in neutralizing shampoos that stops OH ion reactions after relaxing.
Natural fermentation-derived chelator weaker than EDTA.
Polycarboxyl acid that is both AHA and BHA; found in citrus and the Krebs cycle; antioxidant; 20% increased epidermal thickness and dermal GAGs.

US category for products with both cosmetic and drug function (e.g., anti-dandruff shampoo, antiperspirant-deodorant, fluoride toothpaste, SPF moisturizers); must meet both requirements; not allowed in the EU.
Intermediate filament proteins forming keratinocyte cytoskeleton, responsible for mechanical strength and signal transduction; maturation calcium-dependent; decline with aging and pollutants.

Short FDA list (about 8 substances) banned in cosmetics: bithionol, CFC propellants, chloroform, halogenated salicylanilides, methylene chloride, vinyl chloride, zirconium complexes in aerosols, prohibited cattle materials.
Reversible inflammation of the gums with bleeding, associated with plaque accumulation and Gram-negative anaerobes like Fusobacterium nucleatum and Prevotella intermedia.

Most common PHA, from corn sugar; equivalent to glycolic acid on aging attributes with less irritation; chelates metals inhibiting MMPs, reduces UV elastin promoter activation by 50%, and strengthens barrier against SLS.
Derived from sebum hydrolysis; contributes to skin hydration (asebic mice studies).
Carrier (not an effective maceration solvent) from local rapeseed; avoids preservatives by preventing germ growth.
Common humectant whose moisturizing depends on humidity; at low humidity draws water from inner skin.
Humectant that left hair rougher than sodium PCA.
SFDA-sanctioned Gulf standard (equivalent SASO 1953/2009) based on Directive 76/768 with tables of prohibited, restricted substances, colorants, preservatives and UV filters.
Denaturation and bond breakage of hair proteins from heat, perms, bleaching, alkaline straightening, UV and mechanical fatigue, compromising moisture control and mechanical and optical properties.
Adaptation via compatible solutes protecting cells from osmotic stress; offered as therapy for collagen synthesis, inflammation, wrinkles, brightening, age spots and acne.
Phenylalanine-derived polyphenols that absorb UV, repel herbivores, and act as antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, photoprotecting and antimicrobial cosmetic agents.
Yellow to red melanin formed from DOPA-quinone and cysteine via cysteinyldopa; predominates in blond hair.
Yellow to red melanin found mainly in red hair; its synthesis also involves cysteine; less photostable than eumelanin.
Affordable surfactants used as diluent/compatibilizer in water-soluble fragrances.
Sorbitan esters reacted with ethylene oxide; high HLB emulsifiers and solubilizers; reduce eye sting in baby shampoos.
Plant antioxidant performing well in oily phases of formulations.
Nonpolar Rosmarinus officinalis leaf extract (solvent or supercritical CO2) whose activity comes from phenolic diterpenes carnosic acid and carnosol; low-odor/color grades available.
Hair behaves as a thermoset, viscoelastic shape-memory biopolymer: it has a permanent shape that can be temporarily changed and later recovered.
Breakthroughs in skin whitening are highlighted among key ingredient developments.
Achieved via tyrosinase inhibition by algal compounds, peptides and lactic acid.
Very large Asian skin care category (Bihaku in Japan) aiming to lighten skin and dark spots; regarded as equivalent to anti-wrinkle for Caucasians.
ASCs lighten skin dose-dependently, of interest in Eastern markets.
Soaps and special toilet soaps were developed for the military and home front in WWII, partly to reduce dermatitis.

In the US, a product whose nonvolatile matter is mainly alkali salts of fatty acids and sold solely as soap; regulated by CPSC, not FDA, unless it has cosmetic claims or ingredients. Classified as cosmetic in the EU.
The original naturally derived anionic surfactant, used since the Akkadians c. 2800 BCE; made by boiling fats with ashes; soap-stabilized emulsions need pH above 7.
Removes about 70% of SC amino acids and 62% PCA.
Film formers (PVP, VP/VA, acrylates, polyquaterniums, chitosan) that form seam and spot welds between fibers to restrict movement and hold temporary shapes without altering hair memory.
Membrane proteins binding pathogen components (bacterial DNA, LPS, flagellin, beta-glucan) that regulate cytokine production.
Pattern recognition receptors (~11 characterized) on epithelia, keratinocytes and Langerhans cells; activation causes defensin production.
Key lipstick component providing crystalline structure; hard waxes melt over ~3-5°C range, soft waxes over ~10-12°C.
Natural alternative to hydroquinone for hyperpigmentation.
Skin lightener; tyrosinase IC50 33; less effective than ellagic acid and tetrahydrocurcuminoids.
Beta-D-glucopyranoside of hydroquinone from cowberry leaves; reversible competitive tyrosinase inhibitor; QD for Shiseido 1989 at 3%.
Used at 0.5% in the anti-aging cream.
Skin of EP classes V-VII with yellow undertones from higher pheomelanin; prone to pigmentation disorders and acne in normal to oily skin; aging shows as hyperpigmentation rather than wrinkles.

Phenolic meroterpene; psoralen-depleted Sytenol A (~95%) is non-sensitizing; inhibits lipid peroxidation, NF-kB, HIF-1 and iNOS; radical scavenging above vitamin E; retinol-like gene expression; 1% eliminated UV erythema; improves acne and aging signs; stabilizes retinol.
Regression phase lasting ~2-4 weeks in which follicle cells undergo apoptosis and a club fiber forms.
Membrane-bound unit containing DNA and cytoplasm; eukaryotic cells contain organelles and vesicles.
Colorants from mineral, plant or animal sources exempt from FDA batch certification, e.g. iron oxides, titanium dioxide, mica, carmine, zinc oxide.
Stratum corneum barrier lipid secreted via lamellar bodies; rate-limiting enzyme of its synthesis is HMG-CoA reductase.
Major stratum corneum lipid determining permeability barrier; 1% of sebum.
Skin lipid whose synthesis is influenced by Ulkenia extracts.
Glucocorticoid stress hormone; excess breaks down skin collagen (loss 10x greater than other tissues), reduces skin regeneration, disrupts REM; linked to adult acne.
Lifting and buckling of cuticle cells with breakage of CMC cement caused by elongation, blow-drying or hot irons; common at hair tips, partly viscoelastically reversible.
INCI family of cyclic dimethyl siloxanes (D4, D5, D6) that are volatile (heat of vaporization 31 cal/g) and give a dry, silky feel; under environmental/regulatory scrutiny.
Reduced by Boswellin CG under-eye cream.
Reduced by PSP, possibly via increased collagen thickening skin over vessels.
Skin problem linked to poor blood circulation; assessed in Albizia self-assessment.
Antimicrobial host defense peptides discovered mid-1980s, produced by epithelial cells (trachea, bowel, epidermis); also proliferative and anti-inflammatory; overproduced in psoriasis.
UV-induced dimerization of adjacent pyrimidine bases in DNA that can lead to cell death.
Chemical changes in DNA structure producing dysfunction; central to most aging theories.
Alcohol in perfumery; must be denatured in KSA; alcohol-containing mouthwash banned in KSA since 2011.
Biodegradable extraction solvent produced from renewable sugar cane, beet, wheat or corn; recycled by distillation.
Most common organic solvent in hydroalcoholic personal care gels; reduces viscosity of Aristoflex HMB progressively above 20%.
Brown to black melanin formed via indole-5,6-quinone; a poikilopolymer; seen in dark hair.
Brown to black melanin; brown eumelanin in low amounts gives blond hair, dark eumelanin gives dark hair; more photostable than pheomelanin.
Hair fibers out of synchrony with the bundle, from damaged shape memory, cuticle damage raising inter-fiber friction, or static fly-away; common after bleaching and hot ironing.

nodes.label: Gel Structure of the Amorphous Phase

summaries.text: Hydrophilic, hydrogen-bonded part of the amorphous matrix (Feughelman's term) that absorbs water, is plasticized by moisture and stores temporary shapes such as water sets.
Soy isoflavone phytoestrogen binding estrogen receptors (preferring ERβ) with 100-1000 times less activity than estradiol; 0.5-1% topically suggested to inhibit estradiol.
Phytoestrogenic isoflavone demethylating agent inhibiting DNMTs and HDACs and activating HATs; stronger than biochanin A and daidzein.
Moisturizers such as glycerin, propylene glycol, sorbitol, PEG; HA retains water at low and high humidity unlike others.
Hygroscopic materials supplying moisture to SC; e.g., sodium PCA, sodium lactate, proline, glycerin.
Serine proteases co-localized to lamellar bodies that progressively dissolve corneodesmosomes for orderly desquamation.
Serine protease desquamation enzymes (stratum corneum tryptic and chymotryptic enzymes) whose expression is increased by some marine exopolysaccharides.
Family of 15 serine proteases (KLK1-15) in SC; KLK-7 is a candidate desquamation protease.
Probiotic genus (acidophilus, casei, lactis, plantarum, reuteri, rhamnosus, helveticus); L. acidophilus cell wall has lipoteichoic acid and peptidoglycans.
Auto-oxidation of unsaturated oils in three steps (initiation, propagation, termination) causing discoloration, off-odor and instability; principal cause of reduced cosmetic shelf life.
Cutaneous malignant melanoma, about 5% of skin cancers; metastasizes with high mortality once invasive.
Malignant pigmented band in the nail; new or rapidly changing pigmented bands should be evaluated by a dermatologist for biopsy.
Dangerous melanocyte cancer with distinct microRNA signature; miR-203 down-regulation promotes melanogenesis and reduces melanosome transport.
Consists of nail plate, nailbed, medial/lateral/distal nail grooves, epionychium, cuticle and nail root (matrix, lunula). Protects distal digits and enhances tactile sensation and gripping.
Fragrance of essential oils, absolutes, concretes, isolates and fermentation products; 3-10 times more expensive than traditional fragrances with limited odor characters.
Ideation process drawing ideas from outside the organization, e.g. hair care developers using carpet-industry fiber knowledge.
Confidentiality and ownership issues in contract R&D, manufacturing, outsourcing and open innovation; file patents before joint projects.
Methodology leveraging internal and external technology assets to accelerate innovation, relying on transparency and collaboration.
Bad breath; intrinsic mainly from anaerobic bacterial volatile sulfur compounds on tongue and plaque, extrinsic from ingested garlic, cheese, tobacco.
Pal-KTTKS (lysine-threonine-threonine-lysine-serine) by Sederma; 50 ppm significantly reduced periorbital lines vs vehicle; stimulates collagen I, III, IV, fibronectin, elastin and GAG production.
Razor bumps from ingrown curled hairs; listed for Black/African American skin class.
Inhibition of gene expression by small double-stranded RNAs, described by Fire and Mello in C. elegans in 1998 (Nobel Prize 2006).
Suppression of certain genes by sirtuins; loss of this function with age is linked to cancer, Alzheimer's and diabetes.
EU Commission scientific committee issuing ingredient safety opinions and 'Notes of Guidance' (incl. MoS calculation and nanomaterial guidance).
EU scientific committee whose 2010 opinion (SCCS/1241/10) addressed D4 and D5 cyclomethicones.
Touch, vibration and thermal perception most significantly affected by advancing age; vulvar touch thresholds 4.6-fold lower in normoestrogenic vs hypoestrogenic women.
Cosmoperine: hydrogenated black pepper piperine (95%); enhances topical bioavailability (green tea +30%, forskolin +40%, BMDP diffusion in 5 min); non-irritating at 0.01-0.1%.
Certification-exempt color additive (21 CFR 73.2575); nano TiO2 widely used in sunscreens and studied for size-dependent lung inflammation.
Colorant with relatively low oil absorbance.
Micronized inorganic UV blocker pigment wetted by glutamate derivatives.
Toothpastes were among products developed for the military in WWII.
Dentifrice delivering fluoride, anticalculus, antimicrobial, desensitizing and abrasive agents; fluoride toothpastes introduced in the US in the 1950s.
Poloxamers used as solubilizers and gelling agents in oral care.
Silica builds structure and viscosity and gives short texture.
Ultraviolet A irradiation from which Nrf2 protects keratinocytes.
UV band penetrating to the dermis, damaging DNA indirectly via chromophore-generated ROS, activating metalloproteinases and decreasing immune recognition.
Transcription factor promoting MMP/collagenase transcription and reducing fibroblast sensitivity to TGF-beta.
Transcription factor formed upon UV radiation that induces collagenase production.

'Night sleeper' extract with preventive and curative anti-glycation: inhibits BSA glycation ~50%, reduces CML 43%, explant AGEs -23.4%, maintains glyoxalase-1 and proteasome activity; reduces skin fatigue.
Human-relevant non-animal methods (predictive models, in vitro tests, pathway-based toxicity information) increasingly used for cosmetic safety assessment.
Early glycation product formed when reducing sugars react non-enzymatically with protein amino groups.
Example formulation with niacinamide salicylate, ethyl lactate, paeonol, carnosine, arbutin and peptide compound (III).
Roll-ons are difficult emulsions (low viscosity, low pH, high electrolyte); use blends of low/high HLB ethoxylated fatty alcohols.
Product category relying on suspending agents; uses PEGs as co-gelling aids for sticks and cyclomethicones for dry feel.
Disease linked to epigenetic changes, DNA methylation, transcription factor mutations and cytokine malfunction; actives may prevent or, after onset, sometimes worsen malignancy.
HA oligosaccharides sensitize cancer cells to treatment and inhibit pro-tumorigenic signaling of high-MW HA.

Lists the chapters and authors of the Sustainability & Eco-responsibility focus book, including an editor's overview by Alban Muller and chapters on defining sustainability, botanical sustainability, the Herboretum network, local cultures for carbon footprint reduction, plant cell cultures, eco-responsible extraction and green industrial production.

Editor's overview of Part 3.3 on hair. Notes that hair aesthetics are linked to viscoelastic properties of cuticle and cortex, that follicle biology (stem cells, hormones, graying) has advanced, and that hair care is moving to a holistic approach targeting live follicle cells with bioactives.
Exfoliating treatment of varying depth; deep peels require caution in darker skin classes due to hyperpigmentation and keloid risk.

Elongated spindle-shaped cells ~20 µm in diameter and ~100 µm long forming ~90% of hair; they synthesize keratin into intermediate filaments embedded in an amorphous matrix and determine mechanical properties.

US: articles applied to the body for cleansing, beautifying, promoting attractiveness or altering appearance (excluding soap). EU: substances placed on external body parts, teeth or oral mucosa exclusively or mainly to clean, perfume, change appearance, protect, keep in good condition or correct odours.
1976 EU directive based on self-responsibility, replaced by Regulation 1223/2009 in July 2013; model for GSO, Chinese and CU rules.
EU online portal where the Responsible Person must notify products (category, RP, nanomaterials, CMR, frame formulation, label) before market placement; not an authorization.
Linking of polymer chains into a network; higher cross-link density generally raises yield stress and viscosity of rheology modifiers and determines elastomer vs resin behavior in silicones.

Conformity document for 13 higher-risk cosmetic categories (e.g. tanning, whitening, children's, hair dyes, nanomaterial products, peelings, fluoride oral care); issued to manufacturer, unlimited validity, valid across the CU.
Cyclooxygenase-2 inflammatory enzyme inhibited by verbascoside.
Inflammatory mediator modulated by curcuminoids.
Inducible pro-inflammatory enzyme catalyzing prostaglandin biosynthesis from arachidonic acid; triggered by ubiquitinated protein aggregates.
Mineralized dental plaque (tartar), ~80% inorganic (brushite, octacalcium phosphate, whitlockite, apatite) with ~400 ppm fluorine; considered cosmetic but associated with periodontal disease.

Complex heterogeneous microbial biofilm on teeth that develops by ecological succession from Gram-positive cocci to anaerobic and acid-tolerant species; pathogenicity relates to mass and specific microbes.
Pain from exposed dentin triggered by heat, cold, pressure or sugar; affects about one in seven people.
Comprehensive regimen of cell/connective tissue nutrients (glucosamine, amino acids, lecithin, EFAs, vitamins, sirtuin activators); 12 weeks raised ICW in 57.5% of patients.
DHT, formed from testosterone by type II 5-alpha reductase; induces dermal papilla cells to secrete TGF-b1 and DKK-1 inhibiting keratinocyte growth; levels rise with age.
DNMT1 (maintenance, most abundant), DNMT3A and DNMT3B add methyl groups to cytosines.
Repair of UV-induced DNA dimers, e.g., by photolyase via photoreactivation.
Base excision and double-strand break repair aided by SIRT6; immediately affected by sirtuin expression changes.
Green tea catechin associated with Nrf2 activation and reported to activate AMPK.
Predominant dietary flavonoid (EGCG).
EGCG: major tea polyphenol; demethylating agent inhibiting DNMT1 and HATs, modulates miRNA, induces cancer apoptosis.

nodes.label: EU Animal Testing Ban for Cosmetics

summaries.text: EU prohibition (Art. 18 of Regulation 1223/2009) on animal testing of cosmetic products and ingredients and on marketing animal-tested products, fully applicable from March 2013.
Skin phototype scale (I-VI) based on tanning ability and sunburn propensity; NMSC highest in types I and II.
Active ingredients of German chamomile flower; synthesized in chloroplasts.
Over 5000 plant compounds with flavane nucleus; free radical scavengers, UVA absorbing, cytoprotective, anti-inflammatory, inhibit DNA damage; e.g. quercetin, catechin, kaempferol, EGCG.
Exclusive to Coleus forskohlii; direct adenylate cyclase activator raising cAMP and lipolysis without adrenergic activation; ForsLean 95% at 2-5% reduced thigh circumference 9.37% in 54 women.
Coleus forskohlii compound acting as fat mobilizer.
Conversion of gene information into mRNA and then protein; how cells make the right proteins at the right time and quantity.
Most studied plant antioxidants; promising in mice but human trials failed to show visible anti-aging benefit, though elastic tissue improved histologically.
Water-soluble antioxidants whose permeation is enhanced by tetrahydropiperine.
Camellia sinensis catechins (EGCG, EGC, EC) quenching multiple ROS; reduce UV erythema, sunburn cells, Langerhans cell depletion and pyrimidine dimers.
Bulk of the hair shaft made of cortical cells; provides strength, color and texture and is responsible for most mechanical properties.
Permanent straight, wavy or curly hair shape, associated with the ratio and arrangement of ortho- to para-cortical cells and imprinted in the follicle.
Age-related loss of pigmentation, reduced follicle density, more telogen hairs, thinner shafts and slower growth.
Epithelial stem cells residing in the bulge that regenerate the follicle each cycle and supply matrix keratinocytes.
Specular reflection of light from smooth intact cuticle produces shine; lifted cuticles scatter light and make hair dull. Cuticle refractive index is ~1.53.
Inevitable impurities on EU forbidden lists, allowed only in technically unavoidable, nonhazardous traces.
Toxic contaminants some plants fix selectively from soil; soils must be analyzed.
Cell-based screening in 384- or 1536-well plates allowing hundreds of millions of extracts to be tested per 24 hours for new fragrance ingredients.
Acetylation, phosphorylation, methylation and ubiquitination of histones that alter chromatin structure and regulate transcription; acetylation relaxes chromatin, raising transcription.
Acetylation, methylation, phosphorylation, ubiquitination and sumoylation of histone tails altering gene expression; methylation can be inherited.
Fight-or-flight cascade: CRF and vasopressin to pituitary ACTH to adrenal cortisol, epinephrine, norepinephrine; negative feedback by cortisol.

International group of cosmetic regulators from Canada, the EU, Japan and the US promoting regulatory convergence; its topics include animal testing alternatives, in silico models, nanomaterials, trace impurities, endocrine disruptors and allergens.
Property right for intangibles allowing owners to profit or exclude others; mainly a license to sue, a barrier to entry in cosmetics.
ICCR member; Japan Patent Office excludes medical processes, allows post-grant opposition and utility models; deregulated cosmetics in 2001.
Dominates global skin lighteners market; cosmetics industry reported growing at 17% a year.
Major whitening market where quasi-drug approvals and products such as Kanebo, Shiseido, Kose and Pola lines evolved since the 1960s.
Topical eyelash growth products: oil/vitamin formulas (2000s), prostaglandin analogues (2007), then bioactive peptide and adipose stem-cell peptide generations; increase anagen lashes from 20 to 90%.
Enzymatic fat breakdown in adipocytes induced via cAMP.
Lipase hydrolysis of triglycerides to free fatty acids and glycerol, initiated by cAMP-activated lipase.
Branched fatty acid covalently attached to an ultra-high sulfur protein on the epicuticle forming the F layer; provides hair lubricity and hydrophobicity.
Contamination of cosmetics; common limits 1000 cfu/g total aerobic count, 500 cfu/g for eye-area products.
Microphthalmia-associated transcription factor in the cAMP melanogenesis pathway.
Transcription factor for tyrosinase and TYRP1 binding E-box CACGTG; down-regulation prevents tyrosinase activation.
Microphthalmia-associated transcription factor regulating melanogenesis enzyme genes; targeted by miR-25, miR-145 and miR-675.
Organelles with their own DNA that carry out the cell's oxidative metabolism.
Organelles using oxygen to produce energy; weakest link in aging as they lack most cellular free radical defenses.
Nail color change from dyes, smoking, nail varnish tints, artificial nails, psoriasis, Pseudomonas infection, or drugs such as tetracycline and chloroquine.
All-natural aromatic ingredients increasingly demanded but hard to source reliably, often from equatorial regions threatened by global warming.
Seven-step process: idea generation, concept testing, business analysis/marketing planning, product development, market testing, commercialization and evaluation of market results.
Biological entities mediating scent detection; humans have a family of ~350 OR genes, G-protein coupled integral membrane proteins expressed in nasal epithelium cells.
Separation of nail from nailbed due to trauma, infection, dermatitis, psoriasis, drugs and cosmetics such as acrylic nails, formaldehyde hardeners; often colonized by Candida or Pseudomonas.
Preservatives in some OTC vaginal products considered potentially irritating.
Became preservative of choice for antifungal activity; methylparaben most used (13434 US, 54668 Canada listings), plus propyl, butyl, ethyl, isobutyl parabens.

Standardized Phyllanthus emblica fruit extract rich in emblicanins A/B; stable, chelates iron/copper without pro-oxidant activity, inhibits MMPs, increases collagen, lightens skin and reduces fine lines.
Inevitable impurities listed among EU forbidden substances.
Ubiquitous combustion pollutants (e.g., benzo[a]pyrene from exhaust and cigarette smoke) synergistic with UVA in oxidative damage.
Highly toxic contaminants produced by burning fossil fuels; drying equipment must not generate them.
Phenolic free-radical quenchers that delay initiation or slow propagation by donating hydrogen radicals.

WHO: live microorganisms conferring health benefit in adequate amounts; author proposes 'live or dead'; includes Lactobacillus, Bifidobacterium, Saccharomyces boulardii, Streptococcus thermophilus strains.
Compulsory EU dossier (Art. 11) with product description, CPSR, manufacturing/GMP statement, proof of claimed effects and animal testing data; available to authorities.
Degradation of cosmetics by bacteria and fungi (often combined) and chemical instability; can cause infections and lost sales.
Amino acid found with glycine at protein-surface loop locations.
Amino acid uniquely retaining moisture at low humidity, forming with leucine/isoleucine a lipid bilayer that inhibits moisture loss; boosts collagen in cocktail.
Amino acid osmoprotectant; increased tenfold-fivefold under salt stress.
Created 2003, Cosmetic Department since 2008; issues regulations, controls safety, develops standards and runs cosmetovigilance in KSA.
High-energy oxygen species formed in Type II photo-oxidation; quenched by carotenoids.
First ROS formed from triplet excited endogenous photosensitizers under UVA; initiates lipid peroxidation; also generated by organic sunscreens acting as triplet sensitizers.
Skin lightening cosmetics; hydroquinone-free versions are cosmetics in KSA; require CU State Registration; whitening claims make a US drug.
Whitening/brightening creams; about 60% of Indian women use daily; 71% of China's skin care market; Asia-Pacific market projected over $2 billion by 2012.
Highly hygroscopic humectant from cyclized glutamic acid; plumps fine lines, dramatically increases skin elongation and smooths hair better than glycerin or butylene glycol.
Hallmark of photo-aging: accumulation of dystrophic elastic fibers with lysozyme and amyloid P that provide little elasticity.
Dermal matrix damage from chronic photoaging exacerbated by UV-induced elastin promoter activation.
Exposure to sunlight; most damage accumulated during the first 18 years of life; key driver of photodamage and pigmentation.
Non-coding DNA at chromosome ends that maintain genetic integrity; shorten with each division leading to senescence.
Brand distinguishing a company's goods; protected by use and registration, renewable every ten years indefinitely; key test is likelihood of confusion.
Silent epidemic affecting up to 50% of postmenopausal women: thinning, loss of elasticity, decreased vascularity and nerve endings, dryness and inflammation, mainly from hypoestrogenism.
Over 25,000 kinds of photosynthetic organisms without roots, stems or leaves; microalgae (Spirulina, Phormidium, Anacystis) and macroalgae (Laminaria, Fucus, Chondrus, up to 40 m).
Sensitizing substances, notably fragrance components; an ICCR regulatory topic and subject of EU labeling thresholds.
Dermal allergy to fragrance substances; up to 26 fragrance materials are identified as dermal allergens.
Condition the EU's 26-allergen labeling aims to protect consumers against.
Potential risk of growth factors in hypersensitive patients.
Melanocyte-stimulating hormone binding melanocyte receptor, stimulating melanogenesis via cAMP-MITF.
Keratinocyte messenger binding melanocyte receptors to trigger melanin synthesis.

Disulfide cross-linked, non-crystalline protein phase (M phase) surrounding keratin microfibrils, with high- and low-sulfur regions and a water-plasticizable hydrophilic 'gel structure' plus a hydrophobic non-gel structure.
Yeast cell-wall polysaccharide used ~70 years as nutraceutical and skincare additive; identified by DiLuzio as active of zymosan; stimulates immunity via Dectin-1; primary PDB.
So-called BHA products based on salicylic acid.
Synthetic antioxidant, mixture of two isomers, used against rancidity.
Keratolytic clarifying acids whose stinging is reduced by pH adjustment.
Polyphenolic component associated with Nrf2 activation.
Phenylpropanoid that is an excellent oxidative radical scavenger.
Restricting calories (40-60%) extends life span in yeast, worms, flies, mice and primates; not shown to slow aging in humans; practitioners look older facially.
Surfactants with net positive charge; attach to negatively charged hair and skin to condition; high irritation potential.

Extracellular 'cement' gluing cuticle and cortical cells, made of upper and lower beta (lipid) layers and a delta protein layer; the beta-delta junction is the weakest link and a diffusion path into the cortex.
Glues cortex cells of hair together; contains amino acids.
Antimicrobial clinically shown to reduce gingivitis; also inhibits cariogenic bacteria, controls malodor and speeds canker sore healing.
Listed antimicrobial (dihydrochloride, digluconate, acetate).
DNA-protein material of eukaryotic chromosomes organized into nucleosomes; its winding plays a role in gene regulation.
Chromosomal complex of DNA, nucleosomes (eight histones) and RNA.
Liquid endosperm of Cocos nucifera rich in proteins, amino acids, vitamins, growth hormones; Cococin freeze-dried solids support fibroblast proliferation and improved skin elasticity at 1%; use 1-5%.
Hybrid qualitative (field tests, shop-alongs, in-home visits, diaries, focus groups, interviews, in-store intercepts) and quantitative (surveys) testing guiding development.
Crithmum maritimum oil extract with retinoid-like activity without irritation; up-regulates CRABP2, down-regulates desmosome genes, increases exfoliation and reduces sebum and wrinkles.
Regulation of intracellular c-AMP suggested but unproven as lash conditioner mechanism.
Second messenger activating lipase to break down fat and part of melanogenesis signaling.
Second messenger activating lipase; destroyed by phosphodiesterase.
D5 cyclic silicone, the most common D4 replacement and most widely used elastomer solvent; authors expect it may disappear long-term due to consumer sensitivity.
Amino acid whose reactive sulfhydryl oxidizes to form disulfide bonds that maintain folded extracellular proteins.
Sulfur-rich amino acid involved in pheomelanin synthesis; hair is rich in half-cystine.
Powerful antioxidant amino acid that penetrates skin.
Synthetic topical prostaglandin analogue (MD Lash Factor, 2007); increased lash length 1.44-1.94 mm vs 0.63 mm placebo in 4 weeks; non-irritating, nonmutagenic, no IOP change.
'Nonsurgical plastic surgery' using functional appliances to upregulate methylated 'sleepy' genes via mechanotransduction, remodeling craniofacial bone for symmetry and smoother skin.
Anticipated skin-care approach to improve aging skin appearance by targeting epigenetic changes in hydration, barrier repair, ECM renewal, pigmentation and antioxidant capacity.
Colorants (Annex IV), preservatives (Annex V) and UV filters (Annex VI) usable only if listed.

nodes.label: FDA Draft Guidance on Safety of Nanomaterials in Cosmetic Products

summaries.text: 2012 FDA draft guidance noting nanomaterials may affect safety and effectiveness; FDA has no formal definition but refers to materials of roughly 1-100 nm, and recommends tailored testing.
Polymers that extend wear but are often stiff and uncomfortable on lips.
Ingredients capable of forming a continuous film on a surface; rheological film formers stabilize foam and help distribute sunscreen actives.
Brief to the fragrance house with brand overview, psychographic target, olfactive story and mood board, olfactive category, oil cost target, benchmarks, regulatory needs and timeline.

Company specializing solely in fragrance creation, with sales, evaluation, perfumery, applications, analytical, regulatory, marketing and QC departments and a library of tens of thousands of formulas.
Integrated design of bottle, carton, color and name aligned with scent and story so sensory cues communicate the olfactive character and emotional concept.
Catalytic transition metals released from ferritin by UVB superoxide and from sweat; drive iron-catalyzed oxidative stress and NF-kB activation.
Built with long-alkyl-chain cationic surfactant, fatty alcohol for viscosity, and ethoxylated fatty alcohol; usually <10% solids.
Hair care product; amino acid derivatives improve tensile strength (to 93%).

Alkylresorcinol used 80+ years (throat lozenges, GRAS anti-browning); tyrosinase/peroxidase inhibitor superior to hydroquinone and kojic acid; increases glutathione enzymes; anti-glycation (Synovea HR).
HDAC: deacetylates histones tightening chromatin and silencing genes; at least 18 in humans including seven sirtuins.
INCI name for ADSC-derived peptide extract approved by CTFA in September 2006; topical AAPE gave good-to-excellent wrinkle improvement in 47% of subjects.
Highly toxic radical generated from hydrogen peroxide with Fe2+ (Fenton reaction).
Highly reactive species derived from superoxide; initiator of aging.
Destructive cell-signalling chemicals (TNF-alpha, IL-6) that increase systemically with age and contribute to degenerative disease.
Inability to sleep despite opportunity; primary or secondary, onset (>30 min latency) or maintenance; chronic insomnia is a 24-hour hyperarousal disorder with high cortisol and ACTH.
Apoptosis-promoting cytokine whose increased expression is associated with catagen.
Cytokine controlling MMP secretion after initiation by sex hormones.
Cytokine released by GA-treated keratinocytes that up-regulates fibroblast MMP-1/3 and induces IL-6.
Crystalline keratin micro-fibrils (C phase) assembled in cortical cells and bound via disulfide bonds to the amorphous matrix to form macrofibrils; do not swell in water.
Water within the cytosol (cell water volume); must be kept steady for metabolism and youthful appearance; reduced in elderly, especially diseased persons.
Hardening zone of the follicle where hair cells undergo apoptosis and their proteins are cross-linked by disulfide bonds, imprinting the permanent hair shape.
Process by which matrix epidermis forms nail plate, analogous to formation of stratum corneum in epidermis; matrix cells show adult keratinization by week 20 in utero.
Bionic acid of gluconic acid linked to galactose (milk sugar); 8% pH 3.8 matched glycolic acid in anti-aging benefits, reduced MMP9 and alpha-MSH-induced melanin.
Brown alga extract that inhibits lipolysis-limiting factors, rejuvenates senescent fibroblasts restoring collagen synthesis, and reduces wrinkles in vivo after 28 days.
Specialized transitional region between skin and oral mucosa, covered by thin keratinized epithelium on flexible, highly vascular connective tissue.
Substrate for lipstick; thin layer of moisture present; hygroscopic ingredients can dry them.
Yellow-brown 'cellular garbage' age pigment from free radical attack on membranes; excess manifests as aging spots; common in nerve and heart muscle cells.
MoS = NOAEL / SED; per SCCS should exceed 100.
Reactive dicarbonyl glycotoxin (MGO) forming AGEs such as CML/CEL; overproduces H2O2 accelerating fibroblast senescence.
Alcohol-containing mouthwashes banned by SFDA in 2011 because alcohol-free alternatives exist.
Mouthrinse delivering fluoride, antimicrobials or flavors for caries, gingivitis and malodor control.
Increases HA, collagen-1 and elastin in fibroblasts; raised skin thickness 13% in 8 weeks; regimen improved nasolabial folds 10.3% and crow's feet 17.8%.
Germinal tissue (nail root) extending 5-10 mm proximal to the cuticle that produces onychocytes forming the nail plate; plate thickness relates to matrix length.
Keratinized cells originating in the nail matrix, without keratohyalin granules; cuticle formed by proximal nail fold.
Hard part of the nail (corpus unguis) made of hard keratin from dead flattened onychocytes; contains 7-12% moisture, 0.15-0.76% fat and about 9-12% cystine by weight.
Toothpastes and mouthwashes; regulated by separate national standards in China; fluoride products have CU labeling rules.
Neem bark used for antimicrobial oral and dental care.
Harvesting beyond regeneration capacity, threatening species such as Brazil nut and rosewood with extinction.
Unauthorized making, using, selling or importing a patented invention during its term; remedies include injunction and damages.
Breaking disulfide bonds with 7-9% ammonium or sodium thioglycolate at pH ~9.5, winding on rollers, and reoxidizing with 3% hydrogen peroxide to curl hair; quasi-permanent with gradual reversion.
Perming with ammonium thioglycolate neutralized by sodium bromide reduces tensile strength.
U.S. trade association (formerly CTFA) that assigns INCI names and governs botanical and ingredient label naming.
US industry association (formerly CTFA) that manages, publishes and assigns INCI names.
Formerly CTFA; approved INCI name Human Adipocyte Conditioned Media Extract in 2006.
Cosmetics, Toiletries and Fragrance Association (CTFA), cited as major industry regulator.
Contaminants of plant raw materials that must stay below authorized limits; absent in plant cell culture.
UV-induced damage causing lipid oxidation, disulfide cleavage, tryptophan degradation and cysteic acid formation; hair becomes dry, porous, weak, rough and lighter.
High-molecular-weight cationic polymers used for conditioning and thickening; polyquaternium-4, -11 and -37 also used in styling.
Cationic (sometimes nonionic) polymers based on cellulosic or synthetic backbones that condition hair, form protective films, improve slip and stabilize foam.
Ingredient in OTC lubricants that can cause sensitivity in inflamed mucous membranes.
Common moisturizer influenced by relative humidity.
Glaucoma drugs (latanoprost, bimatoprost) with hypertrichotic side effects increasing eyelash length, number and thickness; rare iris pigmentation and periocular darkening.
Very hydrophilic NMF component formed from glutamine; lower in elderly skin, especially deeper in the SC.
PCA; 12% of NMF, formed by cyclizing glutamic acid.
Cationic conditioners providing ease of combing.
Primary conditioning agents in rinse-off conditioners; made by reacting tertiary amine with alkylating agent.
EU chemicals regulation (Registration, Evaluation, Authorisation and Restriction of Chemicals); substances over 1 t/year must be registered with ECHA, polymers and natural substances exempt.
EU chemicals regulation measuring substance environmental impact; cosmetic ingredients comply while food-grade products don't.
EU chemicals regulation under which ethyl methicone is a registered polymer.
Natural or legal EU-established person designated for each cosmetic (Art. 4), responsible for compliance with safety, GMP, PIF, notification, labeling, claims and surveillance (Art. 5).
Halophyte oil extract stimulating aquaporin-8 and aquaporin-3 and increasing urea, filaggrin, NMF and lipids, improving hydration.
Sensory studies by perfumers and naive panels; the gold standard of fragrance creation, required to confirm HTS hits and detect off-notes.
Consumer-perceived attributes such as speed of breakdown, spreadability, cushion, pick-up and skin afterfeel that correlate with rheological measurements.
Gradual return to original shape after perms or relaxers because residual memory in primary/secondary protein structure and crystalline regions is not erased.
Mitochondrial sirtuin activating acetyl-CoA synthetase and SOD2 by deacetylation; decreased by ozone and disrupted by UVB in keratinocytes.

Organ forming the border between organism and environment; prevents dehydration, blocks noxious materials and microbes, cushions shock, regulates temperature. Divided into epidermis, dermis and subcutaneous tissue.
Largest reservoir of HA, holding 50% of total body HA.
Coordinated immune response by keratinocytes and skin-resident immune cells to barrier disruption (UV, trauma, irritants, infection) to maintain homeostasis.
Typical ethoxylated sulfate anionic surfactant.
Ethoxylated anionic surfactant (SLES-2) whose polyoxyalkylene hydrogen bonding hinders large silicone copolyols reaching the surface.
Anionic surfactant (SLES) that removes about 62% of SC amino acids at 10%; damages hair tensile strength when shampooing.
Chinese category of higher-risk cosmetics: hair growth, hair dye, perm, hair removal, breast shaping, fitness, deodorizing, spot removal and sun block; require registration.
Energy required to break through a liquid surface; water is 72.6 dynes/cm while silicones are much lower, giving spreading and dry feel.
Conventional farming controlling inputs of fertilizers and pesticides; most cosmetic plants come from it; requires checks for pesticides, heavy metals, mycotoxins, PAHs.
Lymphocyte present in skin; interferons increase antigen presentation to T-lymphocytes.
Immune cells activated by antigen-presenting Langerhans/dendritic cells; Th1/Th2 clonal expansion yields allergen-specific sensitivity.
Immune cell; low ROS required for survival, high ROS cause apoptosis/necrosis; decline drives immunosenescence.
Resting phase of the follicle (~3 months on scalp, 4-8 months for eyelashes) after which the old hair is shed.
Apoptosis-promoting cytokine whose increased expression is associated with catagen.
Pro-inflammatory cytokine elevated in older skin.
Inflammatory mediator modulated by curcuminoids.
Tumor necrosis factor-alpha, a cytokine contributing to inflammation.
Replacing mineral oils in cosmetics; improved to lower peroxide index, color and odor; cold-pressed oils oxidize less.
Hair displays both elastic and viscous behavior: elastic under rapid deformation, viscous plus delayed recovery under prolonged deformation, owing to crystalline filaments in a plasticizable matrix.
Balance of viscous and elastic components of a material, described by tan δ = G''/G'; tan δ < 1 means elastic dominance; affects at-rest appearance, pick-up and cushion.
Ease of vaporizing a fragrance component, indicated by boiling point and vapor pressure; green, citrus and light fruity notes are most volatile, musks and woods least.

Temporary shape change by wetting to break hydrogen bonds in the gel structure, imposing a shape on rollers and rapidly drying to re-form them; reversed by re-wetting and slowly lost by stress relaxation.
The stress required to initiate flow of a fluid; increasing yield value improves distribution and suspension stability of actives and particles.
Oligoalginate of mannuronic and guluronic acid from Laminaria membrane acting as EGF cofactor to stimulate keratinocyte growth and speed wound healing; zinc-chelated form controls acne.
Nonionic amides from triglycerides and MEA/DEA; manage salt thickening, solubilize fragrance, stabilize foam; DEA disfavored for toxicology.
Highly volatile gas with odor and trigeminal response; at hair-color concentrations fragrance can barely mask it.
Alkalizer in permanent hair color that with H2O2 causes oxidative damage; absent in demi-permanent color.
Zwitterionic surfactants that change charge with pH (cationic at low pH, anionic at alkaline); used to increase mildness in shampoos.
Male sex hormones (e.g., testosterone) of gonadal and adrenal origin that stimulate sebaceous gland activity.
Male hormones that convert vellus to terminal hair in beard/pubic regions but miniaturize frontal scalp follicles in predisposed individuals.
Canker sores: painful 2-10 mm crater-like lesions on tongue and buccal mucosa lasting 5-10 days; autoimmune origin most supported.
Produced from cell membranes by phospholipase A2; oxidized into pro-inflammatory chemicals.
Ancient Indian holistic medicine ('knowledge for long life') using plant-derived ingredients, treating cause not symptom with individualized therapy; ~1200 plants described.
From Boswellia serrata gum resin (Boswellin CG); uniquely dual-inhibit 5-lipoxygenase and human leukocyte elastase; 1% under-eye cream reduced dark circles 86% in 4 weeks.
Plant materials used for marketing or performance rather than odor, from any plant part and solvent; labeled per PCPC nomenclature.
Plant extracts evolved from crude traditional preparations into pure standardized extracts validated by cell and enzyme assays; fastest-developing natural cosmetics segment.
'Mad cow disease'; reason for US ban on prohibited cattle materials and Chinese BSE certificate requirement.
BSE crisis led cosmetics to abandon animal-derived ingredients, reviving interest in plants.
Xanthine that blocks phosphodiesterase, increasing cAMP to mobilize fat.
Adenosine antagonist delaying sleep onset; half-life about 4.9 hours.
Regulates cytokeratin maturation, desmosomal adhesion, keratinocyte proliferation/differentiation and wound healing; bioavailability declines with aging.
Emissions measure; local cultures can contribute to its reduction (chapter by Jean-Marc Seigneuret).
Communication via ligands binding receptors in three stages: reception, transduction and response; signals are endocrine, paracrine or autocrine.
Chemically modified cellulose (cellulose gum, hydroxyethylcellulose, methylcellulose, hydroxypropylcellulose) with salt tolerance, surfactant compatibility and film-forming properties.

nodes.label: Editor's Introduction to the Ingredient Section

summaries.text: Editor's introduction to the 9th edition ingredient section. Highlights breakthrough technologies: biotech/fermentation (land to laboratory), plant stem cells, marine ingredients, skin whitening, and hyaluronic acid advances, with a focus on anti-aging needs of an aging population.
Natural minerals (bentonites, hectorites, magnesium aluminum silicates) used for viscosity, flow control, suspension and emulsion stability; form opaque dispersions and thrive on shear.
Supercritical CO2 extract of Coleus forskohlii rhizome; at 2% as effective as tea tree oil or clindamycin against P. acnes, S. aureus, S. epidermidis.
Tiny fluid-filled canals radiating from the pulp to the dentin surface; when open they cause hypersensitivity.
Bhringraj; Ayurvedic anti-inflammatory ingredient.
Middle East and Central Asia origin; medium-dark olive; seldom burns; hyperpigmentation/melasma, PIH with acne; skin cancer rare; caution with deeper peels and laser.
East and Southeast Asian origin; medium-dark yellow-olive; ages well; prone to hyperpigmentation, melasma and PIH; may react to retinoids and hydroquinone.

South Asian origin (India, Pakistan, Bangladesh); light to dark olive with yellow undertones; rarely burns; hyperpigmentation, melasma, acne, PIH; sensitive to retinoids and hydroquinone; keloid tendency.
Omega-3, -6 and -9 unsaturated fatty acids from seed/nut oils; aesthetic and restorative claims.
Hydrating nutrients included in the cellular water supplement regimen.
Most common lipstick ingredients; thousands possible from different acids and alcohols, from light penetrating to heavy pastes.
Nonionic emulsifiers in creams, roll-ons and conditioners; low and high HLB variants (Steareth-2, Steareth-21, Laureth-23).
Methicone that strongly lowers surface tension of oils and esters; 1.5% in 28.5% soybean oil replaced 30% D5 in an antiperspirant stick; REACH polymer CAS 63148-54-9.
Market requiring labeling of 26 fragrance allergens above threshold levels on cosmetic ingredient labels.
Phased out animal testing for cosmetics, culminating in a 2013 marketing ban on animal-tested products; its Regulation 1223/2009 governs cosmetics.
Cross-linker used with hot irons in 'Brazilian' straightening for almost permanent shape change; potential carcinogen banned in cosmetic use.
Ingredient in some nail hardeners implicated in causing onycholysis.
Stratum corneum lipid component together with ceramides and cholesterol; synthesis rate-limited by acetyl-CoA carboxylase.
Major stratum corneum barrier lipid along with ceramides and cholesterol.
Harman's 1956 theory that ROS cause cumulative oxidative damage driving aging; recent data, e.g. long-lived species with high oxidative damage, question its validity.
Most commonly held theory, proposed by Denham Harman in 1954: free radicals damage molecules causing DNA damage, protein cross-linking and age pigments.
Fermentation lowers CO2 emissions, uses renewable biomass waste, limits fossil fuels and pesticides, and prevents depletion of wild biomass.
Movement toward sustainable, renewable raw materials; silicone is commonly considered not green, so it is used at minimal levels.
Cleavage by enzymatic, free radical, thermal, ultrasonic, acid and alkaline methods; native HA has low enzymatic resistance and short half-life.
Fiber fracture associated with dryness, loss of sebum, chemical relaxer misuse and weak disulfide network.
Results from tensile strength loss after perming (75-95%) and bleaching (90%); mitigated by amino acid derivatives.
Water-based styling product requiring water-soluble fragrance for clarity; key fragrance point is application.
Water-based pseudoplastic styling polymer formulation with high zero-shear yield stress; forms thick uniform seams for extreme styles.
Measure of hair strength reduced by perming, bleaching and shampooing.
Space occupied by a hair bundle beyond its nominal volume while fibers stay aligned in synchrony; created dynamically by water-setting in motion, friction, polymers, back-combing or static.
Canadian authority receiving Cosmetic Notification Forms, maintaining the ingredient hotlist and issuing 2011 working definition of nanomaterial.
Network promoting local cultures and biodiversity, subject of a chapter by Geneviève Bridenne.
HAT: acetylates histones opening chromatin for gene expression; HAT/HDAC imbalance drives aging.
Project that revolutionized molecular biology research; many current techniques and gene-interaction knowledge derive from it.
International project completed 2003 finding only ~20,500 genes (<2% of genome), revealing mutations too rare to explain disease and aging.
HA modified with hydrophobic groups (e.g. 50 kDa HA with 50% hexyl groups) to enhance SC penetration; enhanced hydration comparably to 17 kDa HA; can form micro/nano vehicles.
Family of genetic disorders of dry scaling skin; ichthyosis vulgaris results from abnormal retention of keratinocytes and filaggrin mutations.
Genetic hyperkeratotic disorders with dry scaling skin; first AHA indication.
Older skin has higher interleukin-1, interleukin-6 and TNF-alpha, creating a vicious cycle of inflammation, repair and itching in vulvar skin.
Determined by the degree of consumer behavioral change required, not novelty; most new products are continuous innovations and 'hot' ingredients are merely popular.
Friction between hair fibers balancing bending forces; high friction or polymer welds fix shapes, low friction (silicones) lets fibers slip and recover permanent shape.
Chemical messenger transfer between keratinocytes dependent on desmosomes and cytokeratins; loses efficiency with age.

Golgi-derived secretory organelle (0.1-0.5 micrometers) appearing in the stratum spinosum; secretes lipids, hydrolytic enzymes and antimicrobial peptides at the SG-SC interface; about 985 proteins identified.
Facial laser procedures requiring caution in olive and dark skin classes due to hyperpigmentation and keloid risk.
Omega-6 unsaturated fatty acid found in seed and nut oils.
Omega-6 C18:2 fatty acid that decreases tyrosinase level and accelerates its degradation; QD for Sunstar 2001 at 0.1%.
Phospholipid/cholesterol bilayer vesicle carrier for hydrophilic or lipophilic actives; five proposed mechanisms of SC penetration; conventional liposomes do not penetrate intact.
Vesicle encapsulation that protects photolyase activity and delivers it effectively.
Amino acid positively charged at neutral pH, a major contributor to protein charge.
Essential amino acid needed for collagen; lysine-poor diets may increase wrinkles.
Bionic acid of gluconic acid linked to glucose; increased cell turnover 82% in eight days, reduces lipid peroxidation, nonirritating at 20%.
The 'Original Four' P's - Product, Price, Place and Promotion strategies - that form the foundation of the marketing program, tailored to market segments.
Eye product; CU limits pH 5.5-8.5 and stricter microbiology (<=10^2 CFU/g).
Often stored in hot conditions (purse, car) promoting spoilage.
Pigmented product relying on suspending agents; organoclays and trihydroxystearin control flow.
Immune cell found in the epidermis and dermis.
Mesenchymal dermal cell with heparin and histamine granules; active participant in inflammation and irritation.
Signal peptides released by enzymatic degradation of ECM proteins that act as cell messengers in wound healing and tissue repair; natural and cryptic classes.
Multi-step pathway: transcription to pri-miR, Drosha-DGCR8 microprocessor cleavage to pre-miR, Exportin-5 export, DICER1/TRBP processing to a duplex and loading into RISC.
Pigments in solvents applied to nails; nail polishing dates to 3000 BC in China; repeated use of polish and removers linked to splitting and discoloration.
Requires flow properties so brush marks disappear; organoclays suspend pigments.
Single components removed from essential oils by crystallization or fractional distillation without chemical transformation, e.g. menthol from peppermint oil.
Fluid whose shear stress/shear rate ratio is constant; polydimethylsiloxane is an example; preferred flow for cleansers.

nodes.label: Organisation for Economic Co-operation and Development

summaries.text: Publishes validated test guidelines; OECD-validated alternative tests accepted in EU.
Application of open innovation to sustainability goals; OIS companies collaborate with competitors and NGOs, embrace transparency and share green IP, adopting a more complete OI model.
Reaction products of hydrophilic clays with long-chain quaternary compounds (e.g., quaternium-18 hectorite); highly thixotropic, the first choice to thicken oil-based systems.
Specialist trained 5-10 years by apprenticeship who commits up to 3,000 raw materials to olfactive memory and composes fragrances, typically using 5-15 trials per new fragrance.
Physicochemical parameter specified by CU per category: facial/body cream 5.0-9.0, liquid mascara 5.5-8.5; 33 pH categories.
DNA repair enzyme (EC 4.1.99.3) from Anacystis nidulans activated by visible light; 1% liposomal photolyase reduced UV dimers by 45% in one hour.
Amino acid-derived emollient; 0.5% in shampoo restored bleached hair tensile strength to 95% and wets UV pigments.
Meristem cells maintaining totipotency; cultured callus and suspension cells resemble undifferentiated meristem cells.
Cultured plant cell extracts (apple, jasmine, lilac); distinct from extracts of plant stems.
Formation of abnormal bonds between proteins that reduce mobility and elasticity; cross-linking of collagen responsible for wrinkling.
DNA lesion formed between adjacent pyrimidines by direct UVB absorption, producing UVB signature mutations.
CPDs: most common UV DNA lesions forming at methylation sites; major source of sunlight mutations.
Exotic ingredients from Amazon, Africa and Asia (copaiba balsam, andiroba oil, dragon's blood, açai butter, buriti oil, maracuja oil) adding moisturization, emolliency and shine.
KSA limits: active <=3% in rinse-off hair products, <=2% elsewhere; preservative <0.5%.
Basis of beta hydroxy acid products, usually about 2%.
Natural-source preservative on all positive lists showing excellent results in aqueous systems and emulsions.
Heavily cross-linked silicones with no Si-O-Si rotation forming non-rubbery films; include MQ and MDQ resins.
Contributes to adverse skin effects; sleep resets metabolism, repairs damaged cells and clears waste.
Sorbitol + fatty acids; low HLB emulsifiers; can form liquid crystals; first nonionics (1930s).
Testing of a formula (shelf-aging stability, rapid aging, freeze-thaw, light exposure) until results are satisfactory and the formula is robust under foreseeable conditions.
Fluoride source that also reduces gingivitis, blocks dentinal tubules, and helps control malodor.
SC renewal time, measured by dansyl chloride, increases from 19.8 days (under 35) to 28.1 days (over 60) due to decreased epidermal proliferation.
Acidogenic, acid-tolerant cariogenic plaque bacterium identified as a specific caries pathogen.
Broccoli component found effective via the Nrf2 pathway.
Cruciferous isothiocyanate decreasing DNMTs, inhibiting HDACs, regulating Nrf2 and boosting phase II enzymes.
Enzyme that maintains and rebuilds telomeres; found in germ and cancer cells; telomerase inhibitors may stop cancer cell division.
Shear thinning with delayed recovery: viscosity decreases under shear and recovers only over time after shear is removed.
Intrinsic (within tooth) or extrinsic (chromogens from tea, coffee, tobacco, metal ions) tooth discoloration of cosmetic concern.
Asian (Indian, Chinese) traditional remedies passed orally; documentation safeguards sovereignty against patenting of nonoriginal innovations.
Indigenous knowledge of plant uses (anti-inflammatory, cleansing, sunscreens, wound healing) guiding discovery; must be truthfully represented in marketing.
Antimicrobial not permitted at any concentration in KSA cosmetics.
Antimicrobial clinically demonstrated to reduce gingivitis and useful for oral malodor.
Listed antimicrobial (494 US).
Major intracellular protein degradation system: E1, E2, E3 enzymes tag proteins with ubiquitin for proteasome degradation; controls cell division, signaling, gene regulation.
Market where cosmetic law (since 1938) rests on the responsibility of the firm placing products on the market, with postmarket verification rather than premarket approval.
Diverse country: 2010 census 308.7 million, 63.7% White non-Hispanic single race, 16.3% Hispanic, 12.2% Black, 4.7% Asian.
Pentacyclic triterpenoid from Salvia officinalis; anti-inflammatory; liposomal form increases ceramides and collagen; improves collagen bundles and wrinkles; use 1-5%.
'Patent-lite' in China, Japan, Korea and others; lower inventive step, little examination, about 10 years; not in US.
Most common patent covering products, processes, product-by-process or new uses (e.g., birch bark extract to reduce wrinkles); 20-year term, about 40% acceptance rate.

Phenylpropanoid glycoside (acteoside) containing caffeic acid and hydroxytyrosol; inhibits NF-kB, COX-2, iNOS and activates Nrf2; produced by Syringa vulgaris, Buddleja davidii cell cultures; used for lightening.
Water acts as the natural plasticizer of hair proteins, softening the gel structure of the amorphous phase so less force is needed to deform moist hair.
'WS' fragrance pre-solubilized in surfactant (typically 70-80% polysorbate) for clear water-based products like hair gel; only 20-30% provides odor.
Vacuum drying at <=40 C where water vapor is adsorbed onto 4-angstrom zeolites, whose exothermic reaction heats the product; low energy, no refrigerants, yields native carrier-free extracts.
Certification-exempt color additive (21 CFR 73.2991); restricted in KSA below 25% unless for a medical condition (then a drug).
Inorganic UV blocker pigment.
Ethanol extract of a concrete with waxes removed (or supercritical CO2 extract); used as touch ingredients at 0.001-0.100% for rich odor value.
SNAP-25-derived neurotransmitter-inhibiting peptide with Botox-like effect via SNARE inhibition; anti-wrinkle.
Fat cells whose excessive volume causes cellulite.
Fat cell; adipocyte size reduced by Laminaria extract; cellulite fat lobules are larger in females.
Hypodermal white adipose cells storing energy in lipid droplets; differentiation regulated by microRNAs.
Unfolding of alpha-helical keratin into the beta configuration at 2-35% strain (yield region); reversible when mechanical, usually irreversible when caused by heat or chemicals.
Soft keratin with alpha-helical structure found in hair, nails, skin and wool; unfolds to beta configuration at 2-35% strain.
Modified sulfonic acid (acrylamido-2,2-dimethyl propane sulfonic acid) cross-linked polymers with a permanent pH-independent negative charge that swell in water.
Compounds controlling microbes; Ayurvedic botanicals can serve as natural preservatives.
Alkali-swellable emulsion and hydrophobically modified alkali-swellable emulsion polymers of methacrylic acid and alkyl acrylates, supplied as low-viscosity latex that thickens upon neutralization.
Nanomaterials interfere with optical readouts, dyes, ROS measurement and adsorb nutrients/cytokines, causing false positives or negatives.
Adenosine triphosphate, the chemical energy store common to all organisms.
Cellular energy; decreased in keratinocytes after UVB.
Stimulates collagen I and elastin, inhibits MMP1, activates LOX/LOXL, antioxidant, increases proteasome expression.
Longest-lasting, least volatile and most expensive notes (musks, woods, amber, heavy florals) that support and round a fragrance.
Clay pre-dispersed in solvent as master gel; reduces molecular movement and sweating in lipsticks; rheology control.
Clay based on aluminum silicate; darker than hectorite.
Reservoir of plant molecules for cosmetics; over 300,000 flowering plant species with ~70,000 undiscovered; protecting it is life insurance for humanity and industry.
Third-generation AHAs (aldobionic acids): a monosaccharide linked to an aldonic acid; ~358 Da; very hygroscopic, antioxidant, metal chelating and MMP-inhibiting.
New bone deposition at sutures, cheekbones and mandible supporting skin, reducing wrinkles, sagging and dark circles.
CML: typical AGE; collagen contains three times more CML at age 80 than 20; UV oxidation accelerates CML in actinic elastosis.
Assay using lab cells expressing ORs as miniaturized detectors; reliability depends on mimicking native receptor physiology; typically measures calcium influx with fluorogenic dyes.
Progressive loss of intracellular water with accumulation of dry mass; increases free radical damage efficiency and slows enzymes; final common pathway of aging.
Ester of caffeic and quinic acids; inhibits NF-kB and AP-1, activates Nrf2, decreases chemical carcinogenesis in animal models.
Loss of synchrony of clock genes with earth's cycle due to stress, aging, shift work; induces genome instability, premature aging, cancer, obesity, diabetes.
Peripheral molecular clocks present in nearly all cells (period, clock, cycle, timeless); expressed in human skin cells (shown 2000).

nodes.label: CMR Substances
aliases: carcinogenic, mutagenic or toxic for reproduction

summaries.text: Carcinogenic, mutagenic or reprotoxic substances per Regulation 1272/2008; category 2 banned unless SCCS-approved; 1A/1B banned except strict conditions.
Natural extracts obtained by hydrophobic-solvent extraction of plants, containing essential oil plus waxes; very expensive touch ingredients.
Gly-His-Lys tripeptide identified in human plasma in the 1970s with high Cu2+ affinity; signaling and copper carrier peptide shown to stimulate wound healing and reduce fine lines and wrinkles.
Desmosomes at SC level broken by enzymes to favor desquamation.
Proteins binding corneocytes; AHAs degrade them to decrease cohesion and enhance desquamation.
Rigid, chemically resistant cross-linked protein band with covalently bound omega-hydroxyceramide lipid layer replacing the corneocyte plasma membrane.
Protein-lipid structure of corneocytes attached to keratin scaffold.

CFDA premarket registration required for all imported cosmetics and domestic special-use products, with dossier in simplified Chinese, MOH-accredited lab testing, free sale certificate and BSE certificate; may take months or years.
Strong wax crystalline matrix needed for stick strength; excessive pigment loading turns it amorphous and breaks at cup line.
Flat layered cells ~0.5 µm thick stacked 5-11 deep around the cortex; layers are F-layer (18-MEA), epicuticle, exocuticle, endocuticle and CMC; behavior is viscoelastic and moisture sensitive.
Scalp flaking most common with oily scalps; managed with anti-dandruff shampoos.
Scalp condition caused primarily by Malassezia furfur.
Dissolution of tooth mineral by acid when plaque pH falls below the critical pH.
Skin inflammation that WWII home-front toilet soaps and barrier creams were developed to reduce.
Frequency and severity increased in clock-deficient models.
Cytoplasmic RNase III that processes pre-microRNAs into 20-25 nt duplexes; its knockout in mouse skin disrupts epidermal and hair follicle morphogenesis and causes premature senescence.
DSC detects the hair crystalline melting endotherm and denaturation enthalpy, which drops 30-50% after alkaline relaxers.
DSC estimates non-freezable bound, freezable bound and free water around HA; 650 kDa HA binds 7.6 non-freezable and up to 43 freezable water per disaccharide.
Common fragrance carrier with the most water solubility of common carriers; poorly soluble in bath oils and silicones, forming a second phase in bath oil.
Free radical scavenging measured by absorbance decrease of DPPH radicals at 516 nm.
Inflammatory cytokine assay; metal oxide nanoparticles adsorb cytokines giving false negatives.
Monitors defensin levels in epithelial cultures before/after test candidates; semi-quantitative.
Keratinocyte-derived messenger activating melanocytes.
Progressive deregulation of epigenetic marks with age, exacerbated by UV, smoking, stress, diet, alcohol; visible in twin studies.
EU mandate, based on SCCNFP opinion, that any of 26 dermal allergens present above set levels in a finished product be listed on the ingredient label.
High-MW sugar polymers secreted by marine microorganisms with no land equivalent; used as line fillers, mattifiers, sebum absorbers and exfoliants.
Anionics can cause eye irritation; reduced by carboxylates and polysorbates.
Ocular irritation scored on the Draize scale; lower-MW dimethicone copolyols penetrate the eye and irritate more.
ECM glycoprotein binding integrins and collagen.
ECM protein stimulated by Matrixyl.
Dispersion of gas in a small volume of liquid; anionics give highest foam; no physical role in cleansing but a key consumer cue of luxury.
Wilber-based framework of subjective/objective individual and cultural/societal quadrants explaining consumer response to product degradation and regulation.
EU requirement to label 26 allergens (Annex III 67-92) above 0.001% in leave-on and 0.01% in rinse-off products.
Translates the client's request into an olfactive structure, guides perfumers on trends and impartially critiques creations; likened to a food critic or golf caddy and represents the marketer.
A note or accord is an odor character, almost a mini-fragrance, composed of about 2-20 materials each contributing a facet; fragrances combine several accords.
Industry-standard diagram representing a fragrance's top, middle and base note characters.
Receptor that activates or inhibits an enzyme generating a second messenger or modulates an ion channel.
Class of membrane proteins localized in outer cell membranes; odorant receptors are GPCRs whose activation causes calcium influx.
Regional bloc of Saudi Arabia, Kuwait, UAE, Qatar, Bahrain and Oman; GSO standards apply across it; also a regional patent organization.
Temperature at which a hard amorphous polymer softens; hair Tg ~144°C relates to the amorphous matrix, and styling polymer Tg governs hold versus flaking.
Amino acid that can be acylated into acyl glutamate surfactants, esterified into emollients or cyclized into PCA humectant.
Gupta-Walker osmoprotective anti-senescence peptide derivatives for topical skin anti-aging; formulated at pH 4.5-6.5.
Glyoxalase-1 and -2 enzyme system detoxifying glyoxal/MGO via glutathione; overexpression extends diabetic animal lifespan; reduced by glycation.
Manufacturing quality rules; mandatory for US drugs (21 CFR 210/211) but only guidelines for US cosmetics; mandatory in EU via ISO 22716 (Art. 8).
GMP standards for all products; suspension cell cultures are more GMP-compliant.
Flavor and Extract Manufacturers Association 'Generally Recognized as Safe' flavor designation required for each material in GRAS fragrances.
Safety status that libraries of natural ingredients with history of human consumption and kitchen-like treatments could leverage to facilitate sensory studies.
Generally Recognized as Safe; most sweeteners, flavorings and maskants in lip products are GRAS.
Animal skin sensitization test (GPMT), prohibited in the EU but the only sensitization method accepted by China FDA.
Attaching pendant groups (via carboxyl, hydroxyl or amino) or cross-linking to improve enzymatic resistance, robustness and skin binding; degradation inevitable.
Forms insoluble HA hydrogels with longer residence and robustness; most commercial HA products are cross-linked (e.g. divinyl sulfone in Juvederm).
Region in the lower isthmus/ORS at the arrector pili insertion below the sebaceous gland harboring the follicle stem cell and melanocyte reservoir.
Melting/denaturation temperature of hair's crystalline keratin phase, Tm ~156°C, detected as an endothermic DSC peak.
Measured by sensory and dynamic friction coefficient; reduced by sodium PCA and arginine.
Calcium phosphate mineral making up ~98% of enamel and ~70% of dentin; capable of ion exchange with F-, CO3 2-, Zn2+, Sr2+, Mg2+.
Above 300 mOsm induces secretion of IL-8, IL-6, IL-1beta, TNF-alpha via PP2A methylation shift activating NF-kB.
Loss of pigment when melanocytes no longer function; from overbleaching or trauma from UV, lasers or heat; includes vitiligo and albinism.
Indian patent law excludes cosmetic surgery methods and mere new forms/uses of known substances; has pre- and post-grant opposition; source of TKDL.
Cosmetics industry expected to reach US$3.6 billion by 2014; skin-lightening cream market US$432 million in 2010 growing 18% annually; fair skin rooted in culture and caste.
Transmembrane cell-matrix adhesion receptors also involved in signaling.
Cell-surface receptors mediating ECM signaling; RGD peptides target integrin receptors.
International GMP standard for cosmetics (2007), mandatory under EU Regulation 1223/2009 Art. 8; structure similar to ISO 9001.
Very hydrophobic fragrance carrier that works in oils and silicones and yields homogeneous bath oil, but may not suit sulfate-free shampoo.
Principal fatty acid of coconut oil triglycerides.
C12:0 fatty acid; one of the most notable antimicrobial fatty acids released from sebum.
Heavy-metal impurity detected by FDA in some makeup; CU limit 5.0 mg/kg in products with over 1% natural raw materials.
Natural alternative to hydroquinone for hyperpigmentation.
Yashtimadhu (Glycyrrhiza glabra); Ayurvedic antioxidant.
Plant extract containing glabridin used in many Asian whitening products.
Oxidation of lipids initiated by singlet oxygen and hydroxyl radicals.
Growing plant biomass close to processing facilities to reduce transport and carbon footprint; cultivated plants preferred over wild for identity, safety and sustainability.
Skin sensitization assay (LLNA) recommended under the 3R principle but not accepted by CFDA at the time.
LLNA test negative for delayed dermal sensitization of the lash ingredient.
Fragrance's role of covering the base odor of a product; limited for highly volatile gases with higher vapor pressure than fragrance materials.
Carrier used in spray drying that dilutes actives and adds sugars.
Low-molecular-weight glucose polymer derived from starch that improves body, play time and dispersibility without greatly increasing viscosity; also humectant.

nodes.label: Uttwiler Spatlauber Apple Stem Cell Extract

summaries.text: Swiss apple stem cell extract; 2% delayed senescence in H2O2-treated fibroblasts, prolonged hair follicle growth phase by 4 days and reduced wrinkles in two weeks.
High-MW sugar polymers from algae that retain moisture and form a second skin reducing water loss; can be hydrolyzed into bioactive oligosaccharides.
Surveys, focus groups and other methodologies used to assess consumer needs; intensive market research greatly reduces the marketer's risk.
Proliferating keratinocytes of the bulb matrix that move upward and differentiate into the hair shaft and inner root sheath.
Low-density porous central region of large cuboidal air-filled cells, discontinuous and present mostly in thicker hair; may aid thermal insulation and affects optical properties.
Petroleum-based product that can interfere with condom use and is best avoided.
Hydrocarbon that feels dry with little slip; occlusive and moisturizing but adds little aesthetics; many formulators avoid it.
MicroRNA whose increased expression targets Sox9, Mitf, Tyr, Trp1 and melanosome-transport genes, inducing depigmentation.
Tumor-suppressor senescence-associated microRNA up-regulated in replicative and H2O2-induced senescence; targets SIRT1 and E2F3.
Protein families that stabilize, unfold or assist folding of proteins; part of the cytoprotective stress pathway.
Proteins that attenuate ubiquitinated protein accumulation; proposed for skin aging, inflammation and wound healing.
Amino acid derivatives structurally analogous to AHAs; e.g., N-acetylcysteine, N-acetylhydroxyproline, N-acetyltyrosinamide.
Agricultural polysaccharide thickeners (carrageenan, xanthan, guar, tragacanth, locust bean, karaya, alginates); variable, possible microbial contamination, but pH-stable and salt tolerant.
Azadirachta indica; over 100 actives purified; antimicrobial against S. aureus, E. coli, P. aeruginosa, C. albicans, A. niger; used in oral care.
Neonatal fibroblasts secrete over 110 growth factors, cytokines and matrix proteins; decreased wrinkles and increased epidermal thickness lasting 3 months after stopping.
Fruits, nuts, latexes and other forest products; sustainable harvest levels poorly known for most.
RNAs transcribed from noncoding DNA (about 43% of noncoding DNA is transcribed), including siRNAs, miRNAs, piRNAs, snoRNAs and lncRNAs.
miRNA, siRNA, piRNA and lncRNA epigenetic regulators; a novel ncRNA binds DNMT1 preventing CEBPA methylation.
Most common cancer (about one million new US cases yearly), increasing with cumulative sun exposure; includes BCC and SCC.
DNA repair system whose capacity declines with age.
NER corrects complex damage such as UV-induced cyclobutane pyrimidine dimers.
Minimum air concentration at which a material becomes perceivable; food and decay odors have low thresholds, survival-neutral florals and woods higher ones.
Fungal nail infection, the most common nail condition; four types: distal subungual (most common), superficial white, proximal subungual and candidal.
Cortical cell type absorbing less moisture than para cells; the higher the ortho content the curlier the hair.
