Outermost follicle layer continuous with the epidermal basal layer, generated directly from the bulge; source of VEGF.
Dimethicone copolyol that lowers water surface tension below 30 dynes/cm; low-MW versions more efficient in SLS/SLES systems (RF50 1.2%).
Period genes (PER1-3), first clock gene identified 1971 in flies; PER protein peaks early evening; PER1 and PER2 are tumor suppressors.
Subjective dryness linked more to cuticle surface roughness than to lack of cortical moisture; swatches at high RH scored higher dryness.
Vesicle containing catalase and oxidative enzymes that breaks down toxic hydrogen peroxide and digests fatty acids.
Organelle for hydrogen peroxide metabolism and fatty acid beta-oxidation; its ROS are major contributors to oxidative stress and aging.
Arctangent of reactance/resistance; indicator of cell vitality and membrane integrity; decreases with age; 65% of 40 supplemented patients showed increase.
Physical instability where a product splits into layers (e.g. freeze-thaw) or pearlizers separate; may be solved by changing fragrance carrier.
Anionics made by phosphation of alcohols; emulsifiers in sunscreens, stable over wider pH than soap; rich lubricious foams.
Membrane enclosing each cell containing receptor and transport proteins that let the cell interact with its environment.
Cell membrane that suffers cumulative structural and functional damage with age per the membrane hypothesis.
Sulfuric acid (exhaust, industrial smoke) and nicotine (tobacco) degrade epidermal junctions and cause premature aging.
Antioxidants like vitamin C, E, glutathione and carotenoids can act as pro-oxidants especially with transition metals; vitamin C's pro-oxidant action helps convert proline to hydroxyproline.
Isolated ingredient from a probiotic organism shown to be bioactive (immune-stimulating, anti-inflammatory); INCI names end in ferment, extract or lysate.
PSP from cultured fetal dermal fibroblasts with >100 growth factors and cytokines; reduced periorbital/perioral wrinkles and dark circles.
About 80-90% of new products fail to meet expectations and are deleted within a few years, often due to poor cross-functional cooperation and lack of market research.
Premature aging syndrome caused by lamin A mutations.
Devastating premature aging disease from LMNA point mutation.
Pathogenic microorganism causing acne.
Bacterium involved in acne pathogenesis; topical retinoids do not directly reduce its counts.
Shear thinning with immediate recovery when shear is removed; shown by xanthan and guar gums, carbomers, cellulosics, clays and silicas.
Polyphenolic associated with Nrf2 activation; protects keratinocytes from UVA via Nrf2.
Predominant dietary flavonoid.
Red rice callus culture extract influencing epigenetic aging factors, improving procollagen-1 and dermatopontin expression in vitro.
Applied rheology, the study of flow and deformation of materials, listed among the Editor-in-Chief's areas of technical expertise.
Viscosity measurement with rotational (concentric cylinder, cone-and-plate, parallel plate, Brookfield) and oscillatory rheometers yielding G', G'' and tan δ; requires ±1 °C temperature control.
Product category (e.g. shampoo, body wash) evaluated at bloom, rinse and dry stages; bloom is usually the key evaluation point.
Dynamic cosmetics market with demand growing 5%+ per year (possibly over 15% until 2015); joined WTO in 2012, reducing import duties.
Brewers' yeast, arguably probiotic; yeast cell walls source of beta-glucans.
Produced by three pairs of major glands and minor glands; lubricates, clears harmful materials, buffers via bicarbonate and maintains tooth mineral balance; resting pH 6.5-7.2.
Slow oxidation by chelating metals, quenching singlet oxygen or scavenging oxygen; best combined with primary antioxidants.
Cues through bottle, packaging, color and scent that set consumer expectations and communicate olfactive character and emotional story.
Dimethicone with EO/PO added; powerful W/Si and W/O emulsifiers for foundations and sunscreens.
Mitochondrial sirtuin upregulated by caloric restriction; inhibits glutamate dehydrogenase by ADP-ribosylation, reducing ATP; inversely expressed to SIRT3.
Common salt used to thicken anionic surfactant systems; viscosity rises to a peak then falls (salt curve).
Acyl glutamate anionic surfactant; 10% wash removes only 52% amino acids and 39% PCA vs 62%/56% for SLES and 70%/62% for soap.

Modified starch polymers that build short-textured thixotropic viscosity, stabilize emulsions, prevent syneresis, improve foam and film formation, and are stable to pH, shear, temperature and freeze/thaw.
Granular layer containing keratohyalin granules and abundant lamellar bodies (about 20% of cell volume in uppermost cells); 1 to 10 cell layers thick.
Sucrose reacted with fatty acids (sucrose distearate, palmitate, cocoate); natural, approved food additives; reduce water loss and aid lip adhesion.
Anionics made by sulfating alcohols or alcohol ethoxylates; outstanding foam; ethoxylation decreases irritation and foam.
Extraction of plants with supercritical carbon dioxide yielding absolutes of extremely faithful odor quality.
CO2 above 31°C and 74 bar behaves as gas and liquid; extracts nonpolar compounds from oils/oleoresins; expensive; used for coleus oil.
Master clock in the hypothalamus (~20,000 neurons) receiving light cues via the retina and synchronizing peripheral clocks.
Fragrance materials made by chemical reaction (from crude sulfate turpentine, petroleum or plant molecules); the majority of materials, well characterized, plentiful, cost-stable and not seasonal.
Visible surface blood vessels developing with age from dermal thinning or chronic sun exposure; associated with smoking.
Three-to-four-week conversion of basal keratinocytes into flat corneocytes involving keratin formation, lipid processing, water loss (80-85% to about 35%), and envelope cross-linking.
Cell junctions crucial for the epidermal permeability barrier; Langerhans cells extend dendrites through them.
Second skin barrier in stratum granulosum; claudin-1 and claudin-4 key to barrier; strengthened by beta-catenin.
Divided into enamel-covered crown and cementum-covered root held by periodontal ligaments; humans have 20 primary and 32 secondary teeth.
Removal of stain by abrasives or bleaching with peroxides or chlorine compounds; peroxide oral products not permitted in Canada.

Protection of secret valuable information (formulas, processes, customer lists) without registration or time limit while kept secret; no protection against independent development or reverse engineering.
Drug for melasma that inhibits UV-induced hyperpigmentation by preventing plasminogen binding to keratinocytes; QD for Shiseido 2002.
DNA-binding proteins that switch genes on or off by promoting or blocking transcription; mutations are linked to diabetes, autoimmunity and cancer.
Full disclosure of ingredients, packaging and partners and external auditing; required by both sustainability and open innovation.
Ayurvedic blend of Haritaki (Terminalia chebula), Bibhitaka (Terminalia belerica) and Amalaki; tonic to control microbial infection.

nodes.label: United States Patent and Trademark Office

summaries.text: US office examining patents and trademarks; PAIR system gives access to file wrappers.
Externally visible female genital region composed of mons veneris, labia majora, labia minora and clitoris; richly vascular like the face.
Natural gum that is a good example of a pseudoplastic rheology modifier; synergistic with aluminum magnesium silicate.
Natural pH-stable thickener in auxiliary role.
Compensating people and communities for knowledge leading to commercial plant use, including remuneration and involvement in cultivation.
Pituitary hormone activating adrenal glands; elevated in chronic insomnia.

Under FD&C Act Sec. 601, a cosmetic containing poisonous/deleterious or filthy substances, prepared under insanitary conditions, in a harmful container, or with an unsafe color additive (hair dyes excepted).
Company whose president Alban Muller edited the sustainability book and authored chapters on eco-responsible plant extraction and green industrial production.
Alkyl dimethicone copolyols bearing both alkyl and polyoxyalkylene groups; emulsifiers for O/W and W/O emulsions (e.g., lauryl PEG-8 dimethicone).
Fatty alcohol + glucose; mild foamers, natural alternatives to ethoxylates; decyl, lauryl, cetearyl glucoside.
Fragrance containing none of the 26 EU-labeled allergens above thresholds; excludes natural essential oils, limiting the perfumer's palette.
Acylated, neutralized amino acids (glutamates, glycinates, alaninates, sarcosinates) used as mild cleansing agents.
Hydrophobically modified AMPS polymer (Aristoflex HMB) that thickens and emulsifies high oil loads; higher salt tolerance, slower breakdown and moisturized feel; c* ~1.25% in 62% ethanol.
AHA complexed with arginine or ornithine for slow release; 20% glycolic/arginine took 11 vs 4 days to moderate irritation while 6.3% complex cut SC turnover time 15.7%.
EU list of over 1300 substances prohibited in cosmetics; traces allowed only if technically unavoidable and safe (Art. 17).
Malus domestica meristem cultures improve longevity of skin stem cells by delaying senescence.
Adrenergically controlled muscle bundle that changes the follicle angle and makes hair stand up with cold or emotional stress; absent in eyelashes.
Acrylic or pre-formed nail plates that can cause contact or irritant dermatitis leading to onycholysis and discoloration.
L-ascorbic acid 2-glucoside, QD status to Shiseido in 1994 at 2%.
Ascorbic acid 2-O-alpha-D-glucoside; stable in acidic environments with improved stability and efficacy.
Triterpene from Centella asiatica, perhaps the best natural fibroblast collagen stimulator.
Cellular self-eating pathway degrading long-lived proteins and damaged organelles; takes over when proteasome is overwhelmed; target for detoxifying actives.
Teasing that lifts cuticle cells to interlock fibers, raising friction to create volume; effective but very damaging.
Rate of resting energy use; increased in 55% of supplemented patients, correlating with phase angle (p<0.05).
Ayurveda is argued to pioneer the concept, combining topical treatment with oral supplements.
Concept that hydrating foods and ingestible nutricosmetics protect skin internally from free radical damage.
Mild, good-foaming surfactants classed as amphoteric though technically cationic; from alkylation of tertiary amine with chloroacetic acid.
BIA diagnostic tool measuring TBW, ICW, ECW, basal metabolic rate and phase angle; used on over 1500 patients aged 25-85.
Reference for 'Botox-like' neurotransmitter-inhibiting peptides.
Cholinergic modulator proposed as possible stress-related anti-aging therapy.
Water strongly bound to protein groups that stabilizes keratin secondary structure and remains even at zero RH; its loss with disulfide breakage causes denaturation.
Non-freezable and freezable bound water hydrating HA; 1 g of 650 kDa HA holds 0.8-2 g water; independent of MW from 30-750 kDa.
Petrochemical solvent-carrier for extracts that hinders easy plant waste disposal.
1,3-butylene glycol humectant that increased hair roughness vs sodium PCA.
Calcium ions promote cell adhesion and differentiation genes via calcium-sensing receptor; calcium waves after scratch and via gap junctions direct wound healing.
Microorganism not allowed in 0.1 g (cream) or 0.5 g (mascara) under CU requirements.
Pathogenic yeast controlled by neem extracts.
Hydrogen peroxide-releasing dental bleaching ingredient.
Peroxide bleaching agent in tooth whitening products.
Carrier shuttling long-chain acyl groups into mitochondria for beta-oxidation.
Osmoprotectant; topical carnitine in dry eye offers osmoprotection and modulates immune/inflammatory responses.
Phenolic diterpene in rosemary that rearranges to carnosol upon reacting with radicals, then rosmanol and galdosol, cascading antioxidant capacity.
Used at 0.1% in the anti-aging cream.
Four major classes: enzyme-linked receptors, G-protein-coupled receptors, ion-channel receptors and tyrosine kinase-linked receptors.
Emerging theory that longevity tracks resistance to multiple nonoxidative stressors (heat, heavy metals, xenobiotics), coordinated by Nrf2.
Optimizing intracellular and extracellular tissue water to achieve cellular water homeostasis improves metabolism, health and dermal appearance; about getting water into cells, not just drinking it.
Required per shipment for cosmetics entering KSA (MoCI Decree 6386), issued by approved inspection bodies after document review, testing and inspection.

Biographical note on Meyer R. Rosen, President of Interactive Consulting, Inc. and Editor-in-Chief of Harry's Cosmeticology 9th Ed. It lists his expertise in technical marketing, applied rheology, surface and interfacial chemistry, polymers and organosilicones, and his roles with the SCC, AIC and Euro Cosmetics Magazine.
Higher-risk category requiring CU State Registration and specific labeling; in China subject to 2012 guide minimizing ingredients.

nodes.label: Regulations Concerning the Hygiene Supervision over Cosmetics (1990)

summaries.text: Basis of Chinese cosmetic regulation, defining cosmetics as daily-use chemical products applied to the body surface to clean, deodorize, protect, make up and beautify.
Changing chromatin condensation between open euchromatin and silent heterochromatin; 98% of keratinocyte genome heterochromatic.
Partnering across supply chains, competitors and NGOs; inherent to OI and required by the complexity of sustainability.
